title: The Day After The Rapture - Now What?
speaker: Nathan Bullen
title_alt: The Day After the Rapture: Now What?
summary: In this study, Nathan Bullen explores what the rapture is for and how to be ready. From 1 Thessalonians 4, 2 Peter 3, and Hosea 6 (“in the third day he will raise us up”) he traces God's pattern of sevens and rest: the weekly Sabbath, Pentecost, the sabbatical year, the Jubilee (redemption and return to the lost inheritance, which Israel apparently never kept), and the seventy years of captivity that repaid seventy neglected sabbaths. He notes we stand near the 7,000th year from creation and near a 70th neglected Jubilee, and that Jesus, reading Isaiah 61 in Luke 4, stopped before “the day of vengeance.” He holds to a pre-wrath rapture – a redemptive harvest of those with “a perfect heart an

title: The gods or the God of Heaven
speaker: Jesse Herr
summary: In this sermon, Jesse Herr shows how people press the goodness of God into the service of their idols. At Lystra (Acts 14) the crowd tries to worship Paul and Barnabas, and when the healing cannot be used for idolatry they stone Paul instead – “we must through much tribulation enter into the kingdom.” The Philistines credit Dagon for capturing Samson; Israel credits the golden calf with the exodus; Sodom and its fertile plain feed a devotion to false gods. A nation's gods are its value system, custom-made for its desires, and self-will is short-sighted – it destroys the very thing it seeks, as Sodom's ruin shows. themes: self-will vs. the will of God
keywords: gods or the God of heaven

title: Tree of Life or Tree of Death
speaker: Philip Herr
title_alt: Tree of Life or Tree of Death: Which Are You Choosing?
summary: In this sermon, Philip Herr builds on Mark Bullen's “Now Do You Get It?” Two weeks earlier. God planted the garden, put His man in it, and made its rules; the tree of the knowledge of good and evil was not a gift of conscience but the option to play God – “I will decide what is good and evil” – while the tree of life was obedience to Him. Since God cannot be improved on, any other way is a lesser one, and the forbidden tree should really be called the tree of death. Today God's Word is the way to the tree of life, and the question is which tree you are still choosing. keywords: tree of life or tree of death

title: Mountain Peaks of Prophecy
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Mountain Peaks of Prophecy: Reading the Last Day Up Close
summary: In this multimedia study, Mark Bullen teaches a principle for reading prophecy: from a distance a mountain range looks like one peak, but as you draw near the peaks prove to be far apart. So “the last day” is a last age, and events that seem simultaneous – the resurrection of the just and of the unjust, the coming of the Lord, the meek inheriting the earth – are separated by long spans. He walks Matthew 24 alongside Luke 21 to distinguish the overview of the church age, the AD 70 destruction of Jerusalem (“compassed with armies”), and the still-future coming; reads Daniel 9's seventy weeks without a dispensational gap; and from 1 Thessalonians 4, 2 Thessalonians 2, 1 Corinthians 15, and Reve

title: Now Do You Get It? - God
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Now Do You Get It? The Goodness of God and Repentance
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen preaches on Romans 2, “the goodness of God leadeth thee to repentance,” framed as God repeatedly asking, “Now do you get it?” From Genesis 3 he shows that Adam and Eve could not keep both the tree of the knowledge of good and evil (self-rule, being your own god) and the tree of life; the flaming sword still bars the way until something changes. God uses our own sound judgments against others' sin – traitors, betrayers, a mouse in a trap, a rattlesnake in the yard where the children play – to show us why He cannot simply admit everyone to His kingdom: “you're the rattlesnake.” Ezra and Nehemiah justified God's judgments against themselves; Revelation 21 and 2 Corin
keywords: goodness of God leads to repentance

title: The Father's Blessing - Is It For Sale?
speaker: Nathan Bullen
title_alt: The Spirit of Esau: Selling the Father's Blessing
summary: In this sermon, Nathan Bullen begins with a children's flannelgraph of Jacob and Esau and then preaches from Hebrews 12 on “any profane person, as Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright.” The spirit of Esau, he says, is treating sacred things as common – lightly esteeming what God highly esteems for the sake of relief, comfort, popularity, or security. As children of God we have a Father's blessing and an inheritance incorruptible (1 Peter 1; 2 Peter 1 – partakers of the divine nature; Romans 8 – joint-heirs if we suffer with Him). The question is whether that inheritance is for sale. He names four ways believers sell it: trading communion with God for relief or entertainment,

title: What Vision Drives Your Marriage?
speaker: Jesse Herr
title_alt: The Vision Behind a Godly Marriage
summary: In this sermon, Jesse Herr asks what vision drives a marriage. From Genesis 1-2 he shows that being made in God's image included dominion, the ability to reproduce godliness, and the charge to dress and keep the garden – and that Eve was given to a man with a clear sense of that calling. He contrasts bad help-meet choices (Samson, whose whole vision was “she pleaseth me well”; Ahab, whom Jezebel helped fulfill a godless dream) with good ones (Othniel and Achsah, Ruth and Boaz, Abraham and Sarah), where a man committed to a noble, God-given vision is joined by a woman eager to empower it. title: Our Record Before God
speaker: Philip Herr
title_alt: A Redacted Record: What Justification Really Means
summary: In this sermon, Philip Herr corrects the popular idea that “justified” means “just as if I'd never sinned.” From Romans 4 he shows that Abraham was declared righteous through faith without having earned a perfect record. Using the image of a redacted document, he explains that to have your sins “covered” means they are paid for and blacked out, leaving a record you can present to God – which is why confession and settling out of court matter (Matthew 5:25; 1 John 1:9). title: 1Tim 4:8-16 In Doing This Thou Shalt Both Save Thyself And Them That Hear Thee
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Exercising Godliness for Salvation
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of godliness and its connection to salvation, highlighting that true faith must be active and ongoing. He argues that godliness is not merely a past event but a continuous exercise that leads to the promise of eternal life. The key takeaway is that believers must actively pursue godliness and live in a way that reflects their faith to both save themselves and influence others positively.

title: 1Tim 3:8 To 4:8 How Much Do We Care About Truth?
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Church as the Pillar and Ground of Truth
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of truth within the church, highlighting the roles of bishops and deacons as stewards of God's truth. He argues that the church must adhere to sound doctrine and maintain its status as the pillar and ground of truth, warning against the dangers of false teachings and the consequences of neglecting this responsibility. The takeaway is a call for believers to prioritize the preservation of biblical truth and to actively engage in upholding it within their communities.

title: 1Ti 2:9-3:7 "Father's Day Message"
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding God-Given Roles: A Father's Day Reflection
summary: In this Father's Day sermon, Mark Bullen discusses the biblical roles of men and women, emphasizing the importance of fathers and the office of Bishop. He argues that God has designed specific roles for men and women, with men as leaders and women as helpers, and highlights the dangers of deviating from these roles. The takeaway is that fulfilling God-given roles leads to safety and protection for families and communities.

title: Who Owns You?
speaker: Titus Bullen
title_alt: Surrendering Self: Finding Freedom in Christ
summary: In this sermon, Titus Bullen explores the concept of ownership in the Christian life, emphasizing that true freedom comes from surrendering oneself to Christ. He challenges listeners to evaluate whether they are living in fear, trying to secure their own futures, or in faith, trusting God to provide. The key takeaway is that by being crucified with Christ, believers can live a life free from the burdens of self-ownership and fear, focusing instead on seeking God's kingdom and righteousness.

title: 1Ti 1:17- 2:8 Good Warfare Or Shipwreck
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Navigating Faith: Avoiding Spiritual Shipwreck
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of holding fast to the faith once delivered to the saints, using Paul's charge to Timothy as a framework. He warns against the dangers of straying from sound doctrine, illustrated by the examples of Hymenaeus and Alexander, who made shipwreck of their faith. The key takeaway is the necessity of maintaining a good conscience and integrity in one's faith journey to avoid spiritual shipwreck.

title: 1Ti 1 5 16 God's Law Used Lawfully
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Law's True Purpose: Love and Righteousness
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the proper use of God's law as outlined in 1 Timothy 1:5-16, emphasizing that the law's ultimate goal is love and charity from a pure heart. He critiques the misuse of the law by false teachers who distort its purpose, arguing that the law should not hinder righteousness or love but rather guide believers in understanding God's priorities. The takeaway is that the law is meant to promote God's love and righteousness, not to impose burdens that detract from true devotion.

title: Just Kill That Fly
speaker: Nathan Bullen
title_alt: Confronting the Flies: Finding True Peace
summary: In this sermon, Nathan Bullen emphasizes the importance of recognizing the 'day of visitation' when God presents truth and calls for change in our lives. He uses the metaphor of dealing with a persistent fly to illustrate the necessity of confronting our sins and old habits to achieve true peace with God. The key takeaway is that lasting peace requires active faith and the willingness to crucify the old man, rather than simply seeking temporary comfort.

title: 1Tim. 1:1-7 The Goal Of Our Labors
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Guarding the Faith: The Charge to Timothy
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the importance of maintaining sound doctrine as emphasized in 1 Timothy 1:1-7. He discusses Paul's charge to Timothy to guard against false teachings and the necessity of adhering to the faith once delivered to the saints. The key takeaway is that love, a pure heart, and a good conscience are the ultimate goals of our labor in ministry, and we must be vigilant against doctrines that deviate from biblical truth.

title: Why Would Jesus Say, Depart From Me?
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Narrow Path: Understanding Jesus' Call
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the significance of Jesus' warning to those who claim to know Him but do not follow His teachings. He emphasizes the importance of understanding the narrow path that leads to life, contrasting it with the broad way that leads to destruction. The key takeaway is the necessity of actively seeking and aligning one's life with God's will, rather than assuming salvation based on past decisions or mere verbal acknowledgment of faith.

title: There May Be A Third Option
speaker: Philip Herr
title_alt: Finding Balance: The Third Option in Life
summary: In this sermon, Philip Herr explores the idea that oversimplifying choices can lead to missing important middle ground, particularly in the context of spiritual and material needs. He emphasizes that there are often three categories of existence—lack, sufficiency, and excess—rather than just two. The key takeaway is the importance of recognizing these categories to live a balanced life that honors God, avoiding both the pitfalls of poverty and the distractions of excess.

title: The Person You Don't Want To Be
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Avoiding the Trap of Prejudice
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen discusses the dangers of prejudice and the importance of examining our beliefs and judgments. He uses the example of the Pharisees' rejection of Jesus based on their preconceived notions about his origins to illustrate how easily we can become anchored in false beliefs. The key takeaway is the need for self-reflection and the willingness to challenge our assumptions to avoid becoming the person who sabotages our own growth and understanding.

title: What Does Devour Mean?
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Art of Spiritual Vigilance: Understanding Devour
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the meaning of 'devour' as it relates to spiritual warfare and the nature of evil. He emphasizes the need for Christians to be both wise and innocent, drawing from Matthew 10:16, and warns against the deceptive tactics of the devil, who seeks to absorb and corrupt believers' potential for God's glory. The key takeaway is the importance of maintaining pure motives while being shrewd and vigilant in the face of spiritual dangers.

title: Divine Gratitude
speaker: Nathan Bullen
title_alt: Responding to Divine Love: The Call to Gratitude
summary: In this sermon, following three Sundays of meditations on Christ's death and resurrection, Nathan Bullen preaches on 'divine gratitude' — divine love's response to divine love's gift. Just as God's love, seen at the cross, takes in the whole picture, so a heart filled with the divine nature should begin to emit a gratitude that grasps how undeserving we are and answers with total surrender — 'your reasonable service' (Romans 12:1). The center of the message is the faith of Abraham in Genesis 22: Isaac was not a picture of sin to be given up but the dearest, God-given treasure Abraham was right to protect — until the Owner Himself, the One who did not withhold His own Son, asked for him. Ever

title: The Sacred Seasons Of God
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding God's Sacred Seasons
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the significance of sacred seasons in God's design, particularly focusing on the month of Nisan and its events leading to the Passover and the resurrection of Jesus. He emphasizes the importance of understanding these patterns as they reveal God's orchestration of history and His covenant with His people. The key takeaway is that God's timing and design are intentional, and believers are called to recognize and honor these sacred seasons in their faith journey.

title: Born Again What Jesus Meant
speaker: Philip Herr
title_alt: Understanding Spiritual Rebirth: The Necessity of Being Born Again
summary: In this sermon, Philip Herr answers Nicodemus's question — what did Jesus mean by 'born again' (John 3) — insisting it is an Old Testament truth Nicodemus should have known. Using a simple drawing of a line between the 'wrong side' and the 'right side' of God's law (which he stresses is God Himself — His opinions and verdicts), he traces it from the fall in Genesis 3 (Adam and Eve were not content with the realm God gave them and trespassed the boundary, so all are born on the wrong side) to the new heaven and earth of Revelation 21, which God wants to fill only with people who will stay within His boundaries. From Ezekiel 18 and 36, Psalm 51, Luke 11, and Jeremiah 31 he lays out the two par

title: Rejoicing The Heart Of The Father
speaker: Nathan Bullen
title_alt: The Testing of the Heart: Rejoicing God
summary: In this sermon, from 2 Chronicles 32:31 — 'God left him, to try him, that he might know all that was in his heart' — Nathan Bullen describes a spiritual opportunity that comes repeatedly in a believer's life: the moment when, after God has trained him in some area through preaching, conviction, and the authorities He has placed over him, God steps back and removes the pressure to see whether the divine nature is now alive from within and his appetites have actually changed. He drives the point home with seven pictures — the mechanic turning the key on a rebuilt engine, the foreman stepping back from a new hand, the farmer watching for the seed to sprout, the teacher handing over the pencil,

title: What Bible Says Vs What You Want It To Say
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding God's Word: Beyond Personal Interpretation
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of accurately interpreting the Bible rather than projecting personal desires onto its teachings. He argues that many people fail to grasp the true message of Scripture due to preconceived notions and emotional assumptions. The key takeaway is that one's understanding of God and righteousness must align with biblical truth, as personal interpretations can lead to spiritual deception and ultimately judgment.

title: Working The Road Of Reconciliation With God
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Navigating the Road to Reconciliation with God
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of preparing a spiritual highway for reconciliation with God, drawing parallels between physical road construction and the need for personal spiritual growth. He discusses the obstacles in our lives—represented by low spots, high spots, crooked areas, and rough patches—that hinder our relationship with God and allow Satan to gain a foothold. The takeaway is that by addressing these areas, we can facilitate reconciliation with God and strengthen our spiritual resilience against temptation.

title: Josiah's Story & My Story
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Choosing Righteousness: Lessons from Josiah's Reign
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen draws parallels between the story of King Josiah and his own life, emphasizing the importance of personal choices in the face of societal corruption. Josiah, who became king at a young age, chose to seek the Lord and lead his people back to righteousness despite the negative influences around him. The key takeaway is that individuals, regardless of their background or circumstances, have the power to choose their path and emulate godly examples.

title: Sanctify The Sacrifice
speaker: Titus Bullen
title_alt: The Cost of True Sacrifice
summary: In this evening message, preaching from 1 Chronicles 21:24 — David's refusal to offer God 'that which cost me nothing' — Titus Bullen urges a fresh way to bring our struggles to the Lord: not only 'I can't handle this, help me,' but 'I am a living sacrifice (Romans 12:1); I am giving this to You, and the more it costs me, the more special it is in Your sight.' A real relationship must be reciprocal, he argues, so every hard thing God allows us to bear for Him is an invitation to go deeper. Using the sore muscles that follow a workout, Amy Carmichael's poem 'No Scar?', the widow's two mites, Mary's alabaster box, and a friend's hundred-hour handmade gift, he presses each hearer to take the mo

title: The Law Of The House
speaker: Nathan Bullen
title_alt: Guardians of Holiness: The Law of God's House
summary: In 'The Law Of The House,' Nathan Bullen emphasizes the importance of holiness in the life of a believer, drawing parallels between the ancient temple and the believer's body as the new temple of God. He warns that corruption and unholiness lead to the departure of God's glory, urging listeners to guard their spiritual lives diligently. The key takeaway is that every aspect of a believer's life must be dedicated to God, as the law of His house demands holiness.

title: Divorce & Remarriage: How Not To Test Positive For [Willful Ignorance]
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding Divorce and Remarriage in Light of Scripture
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen addresses the topic of divorce and remarriage, emphasizing the importance of adhering to God's law and the teachings of Jesus. He argues against the willful ignorance prevalent in society and within the church regarding the interpretation of scripture, particularly concerning the permanence of marriage. The key takeaway is that true obedience to God's commandments is essential for entering the kingdom of heaven, and that misinterpretations can lead to spiritual consequences.

title: What Is Worship?
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Heart of True Worship
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the true meaning of worship, emphasizing that it goes beyond mere physical posture to encompass the posture of the heart. He examines biblical examples, particularly from Exodus, to illustrate how the Israelites corrupted their worship by creating a golden calf, demonstrating that true worship must align with God's ethics and character. The key takeaway is that worship involves a proper relationship with God, characterized by reverence, obedience, and a commitment to His ways.

title: The Prize Of The High Calling Of God
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Beyond Forgiveness: Pursuing the High Calling of God
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of moving beyond mere forgiveness of sins to pursue a deeper relationship with God characterized by sanctification and holiness. He argues that many Christians mistakenly focus solely on being forgiven, neglecting the call to live a life that honors God and seeks an inheritance among the sanctified. The takeaway is that true faith involves a commitment to growth and obedience, striving toward the high calling of God in Christ Jesus.

title: What Will You Do With Jesus?
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Choice of Rejection: Humanity's War Against God
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores humanity's rejection of God, tracing it from the Garden of Eden to the crucifixion of Jesus. He emphasizes that the fall of man was a choice to disobey God, leading to a history of sin and rebellion against divine authority. The key takeaway is the importance of recognizing our own tendencies to reject God and the necessity of commitment to truth, even in the face of societal pressure.

title: Demonstration Evangelism: The Hard Truth
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Raising a Moldable Generation for Effective Evangelism
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen discusses the challenges of demonstration evangelism, emphasizing the need to raise a new generation that is moldable and receptive to God's truth. He illustrates how the Israelites, despite witnessing miraculous events, quickly reverted to their old ways, highlighting the difficulty of converting those entrenched in their ideologies. The takeaway is that effective evangelism often requires focusing on younger generations who can be shaped by biblical principles, rather than relying on those who are set in their ways.

title: Demonstration Evangelism
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Living Witness: The Call to Demonstration Evangelism
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the concept of 'demonstration evangelism,' arguing that God desires a people who exemplify His ways to the world. He illustrates how Israel was meant to be a living example of God's statutes and judgments, providing a clear witness to the nations. The takeaway is that true evangelism is not just about preaching but living out the principles of God's Word, allowing others to see the transformative power of faith in action.

title: How Do I Give Thanks In Everything?
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Gratitude in the Midst of Trials
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the biblical command to give thanks in everything, emphasizing that it does not mean being thankful for every situation, especially negative ones. He argues that true gratitude is directed towards God amidst life's challenges and injustices, and that a right relationship with God is essential for cultivating a thankful heart. The key takeaway is that while we may not be thankful for specific hardships, we can always find reasons to be grateful to God for His presence and promises in our lives.

title: Gratitude: Loving The Gift? Or The Giver?
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The True Nature of Gratitude: Honoring the Giver
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of gratitude, arguing that true gratitude is not merely enjoying gifts but recognizing the giver and reciprocating appropriately. He warns that ingratitude leads to ungodliness and a lack of character, illustrating this with biblical examples from Romans and Exodus. The key takeaway is that gratitude involves a sense of obligation to honor the giver, which is foundational for developing good character.

title: My Yoke Is Easy
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Lightness of Christ's Yoke
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the concept of Jesus' yoke being easy and His burden light, contrasting it with the heavy yokes imposed by religious leaders of His time. He emphasizes that every person must choose a yoke in life, whether it be one of sin, societal pressure, or the teachings of Christ. The key takeaway is that while all paths require effort, the yoke of Christ offers true rest and fulfillment, leading to a deeper understanding of the Heavenly Father.

title: Candlestick Qualifications
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Qualifications of the Lord's Candlesticks
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen discusses the qualifications for being one of the Lord's candlesticks, emphasizing the importance of maintaining one's first love and works in faith. He draws parallels between the early church and modern congregations, highlighting that true candlesticks are not merely buildings but assemblies that uphold God's law and purpose. The takeaway is that churches must reflect the passion and purpose for which Christ fought, ensuring they are aligned with His will to remain qualified as His representatives.

title: This Genea Shall Endure
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Enduring Faith: Understanding 'This Generation'
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the meaning of 'this generation' as mentioned in the Gospels of Matthew, Mark, and Luke, arguing that it refers not to a specific time frame but to a class of people, namely the elect who endure in faith. He emphasizes that this group will exist until all prophesied events are fulfilled, and their preservation is linked to the endurance of Christ's words. The key takeaway is the importance of being part of this enduring class of believers, who will witness the fulfillment of God's promises.

title: Wisdom Beyond Your Years
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Cultivating Wisdom for Eternal Impact
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of cultivating wisdom beyond one's years, which is not solely determined by age but by the application of knowledge and foresight in decision-making. He outlines key characteristics of wisdom, including mature decision-making, empathy, emotional regulation, humility, and the ability to learn from experiences. The takeaway is that pursuing this kind of wisdom is essential for spiritual growth and preparing for eternity, as it influences how one interacts with others and navigates life's challenges.

title: Is It The Preacher's Business?
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Importance of Accountability in Faith
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the importance of accountability within the church and the consequences of disregarding God's authority, as illustrated through the story of Ezra and the Israelites. He emphasizes that faith is not a personal matter but involves a communal responsibility to adhere to God's commandments and the authority structures He has established. The key takeaway is that believers must seek a good report from their spiritual leaders and be willing to align their lives with God's standards, rather than living as if their faith is solely a private affair.

title: What More Can He Say
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Vital Connection Between God and His Word
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the inseparable relationship between loving God and loving His Word, as illustrated in Deuteronomy. He argues that true faith manifests in obedience to God's commandments, which leads to blessings, while disobedience results in curses. The takeaway is that understanding and valuing Scripture is essential for a faithful life, and neglecting it can lead to spiritual downfall.

title: The Great Commission And Missions
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Great Commission: A Call to True Missions
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of the Great Commission and its application to missions, arguing that the apostles were tasked with teaching all nations to observe God's commandments. He critiques modern missionary practices that prioritize cultural relevance over biblical truth, asserting that true evangelism involves teaching the moral aspects of God's law. The takeaway is that effective missions should focus on reconciling people with God through the proper understanding and observance of Scripture.

title: Did Jesus Die A Sinner Or Spotless Lamb
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The True Nature of Christ's Atonement
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the theological implications of whether Jesus died as a sinner or as the spotless Lamb of God. He argues that many teachings in Christendom misinterpret the nature of Jesus' atonement, suggesting that He was made a sin offering rather than taking on the guilt of sin. The key takeaway is the importance of understanding the true nature of atonement and the necessity of obedience in maintaining a relationship with God.

title: A Man After God's Own Heart
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Loving God First: The Heart of a True Believer
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of truly loving God with all one's heart, soul, mind, and strength, as exemplified by David, a man after God's own heart. He critiques modern Christianity's tendency to prioritize loving people over loving God, highlighting the dangers of superficial faith that honors God with lips but not with the heart. The key takeaway is the call for believers to examine their own hearts and ensure their love for God is genuine and prioritized above all else.

title: The Mystery Of Anomia
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding the Spirit of Anomia
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen addresses the concept of 'anomia,' or lawlessness, emphasizing its insidious influence on individuals and the church. He draws parallels between natural examples of manipulation in nature and the spiritual deception that leads people away from God's truth. The key takeaway is the importance of recognizing and resisting the spirit of anomia to maintain a genuine relationship with God and adhere to His commandments.

title: The Truth Train!
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Riding the Truth Train: The Importance of True Doctrine
summary: In this sermon titled 'The Truth Train!', Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of seeking and adhering to the truth, as exemplified by Jesus' trial before Pilate. He argues that many people are deceived by false doctrines and that understanding and following the true gospel is crucial for salvation. The takeaway is that believers must prioritize truth over popularity or personal comfort, as it ultimately shapes their destiny and identity.

title: When The Failure Is YOU!
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Embracing Failure: Lessons from David, Peter, and Saul
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the theme of personal failure through the biblical examples of David, Peter, and Saul. He emphasizes that even great figures in the Bible faced significant failures, yet they were able to recover and continue their journeys with God. The main takeaway is that acknowledging our failures and seeking forgiveness allows us to move forward and fulfill our purpose, despite past mistakes.

title: Let's Talk About Communion
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding the True Meaning of Communion
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen discusses the significance of Communion, emphasizing its symbolic nature rather than a literal transformation of bread and wine into the body and blood of Christ. He argues against the doctrine of transubstantiation, asserting that Jesus intended Communion as a remembrance of His sacrifice rather than a re-sacrifice. The key takeaway is the importance of understanding Communion as a solemn act of remembrance that should be observed with reverence and clarity of its meaning.

title: Turning The Hearts Of The Children To...a Goddess?
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Turning Hearts Back to the Father
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of recognizing and combating the tactics of Satan, particularly how he uses goddesses to divert worship from God the Father. He draws parallels between the biblical accounts of Adam and Eve and the historical worship of goddesses in Israel, warning against the dangers of allowing false idols to influence the hearts of children. The key takeaway is the necessity of knitting children's hearts to God through His Word to prepare them for a faithful life.

title: How The Bereans Failed
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Bereans: A Call to Personal Scripture Engagement
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the contrasting responses of the Bereans to the teachings of Paul and Silas, highlighting the failure of some to search the Scriptures independently and instead rely on the corrupt establishment. He emphasizes the importance of personal engagement with the Bible over blind trust in religious authorities, arguing that true understanding comes from diligent study of God's Word. The takeaway is a call to prioritize Scripture in discerning truth over established interpretations that may be compromised.

title: Contending For The Faith - 101
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Guardians of the Faith: Unity in Truth
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of adhering strictly to Scripture and warns against the dangers of self-advancement and division within the church. He highlights how the apostles struggled with understanding Jesus' teachings, often prioritizing their own concerns over His message. Bullen argues that unnecessary divisions arise when individuals go beyond biblical teachings to promote personal agendas, ultimately urging listeners to focus on God's truth and the unity of the faith.

title: Wisdom Crieth
speaker: Philip Herr
title_alt: The Call of Wisdom
summary: In this sermon, Philip Herr emphasizes the importance of wisdom as a divine gift that is accessible to everyone. He argues that wisdom requires active practice and self-discipline, rather than mere acknowledgment, and warns against the consequences of rejecting wisdom. The takeaway is that embracing and exercising wisdom leads to a fulfilling life, while neglecting it results in regret and negative outcomes.

title: Thinking Right In Romans 16
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Guarding Against False Teachings in the Church
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen discusses Romans 16, emphasizing the importance of adhering to the apostolic doctrine and avoiding false teachers who promote divisions within the church. He warns against the dangers of being deceived by those who use persuasive words to lead believers astray, stressing that true authority comes from the teachings of the apostles rather than from church traditions or leaders. The key takeaway is the necessity for Christians to be vigilant in their faith and to stand firm against heresy, ensuring they follow the teachings that have been faithfully passed down from the apostles.

title: Thinking Right In Romans 15
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Strength in Service: Bearing One Another's Burdens
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of using one's strength to support the weak in faith, as outlined in Romans 15. He argues that true strength is demonstrated through self-sacrifice and serving others, rather than seeking personal comfort or approval. The key takeaway is that Christians are called to bear one another's burdens and to please God by edifying their neighbors, reflecting Christ's example of humility and service.

title: Thinking Right In Romans 14
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Prioritizing God's Love in Christian Fellowship
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of understanding and prioritizing God's love in the context of Christian fellowship, particularly between Jewish and Gentile believers. He discusses how differing scruples and practices can lead to disputes within the church, urging believers to grow in love and maturity rather than judge one another. The key takeaway is that true maturity in faith involves recognizing God's priorities of love and acting accordingly towards others, fostering unity and grace within the body of Christ.

title: Thinking Right In Romans 13:8-14
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Love and the Law: Understanding Romans 13
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of understanding the relationship between love and God's law, particularly as outlined in Romans 13:8-14. He argues against the common misconception that love alone fulfills the law, asserting that true love must be defined by obedience to God's commandments. The takeaway is that love is not a replacement for the law but rather a fulfillment of it, requiring adherence to God's moral standards.

title: Thinking Right In Romans 13:1-10
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: God's Authority and Human Government
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of recognizing and submitting to God-ordained authorities as outlined in Romans 13:1-10. He argues that while God is sovereign over all, human authorities are established to maintain order and justice, and Christians are called to influence these authorities positively. The key takeaway is that believers should engage with their governments and societal structures to uphold God's standards, rather than adopting a passive or fatalistic attitude towards authority.

title: Thinking Right In Romans 12:14-21
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Living as God's Ambassadors: Responding to Persecution
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of knowing and adhering to God's Word to avoid deception in a world filled with false teachings. He explores Romans 12:14-21, urging believers to respond to persecution with kindness and to represent God accurately in their actions. The key takeaway is that Christians must discern God's will and act as His ambassadors, maintaining doctrinal purity and integrity in their relationships with others, even those who oppose them.

title: Thinking Right In Romans 12:1-13
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Living Sacrifices: Transforming Our Minds and Bodies for God
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores Romans 12:1-13, emphasizing the necessity of presenting oneself as a living sacrifice to God. He argues that true reconciliation with God requires complete submission and obedience, aligning one's life with God's will rather than conforming to worldly values. The key takeaway is that believers must undergo a transformation of the mind to discern and pursue God's perfect will, actively engaging in self-discipline and stewardship of their bodies for God's service.

title: Thinking Right In Romans 11:21-36
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Balance of God's Goodness and Severity
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores Romans 11:21-36, emphasizing the themes of God's goodness and severity. He argues that while God's grace is available to all, individuals must actively choose to continue in His goodness to avoid being cut off. The message highlights the importance of faith, obedience, and the necessity of understanding the balance between God's kindness and His judgment.

title: Thinking Right In Romans 11:1-21
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Faithful Remnant: Understanding Romans 11
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores Romans 11, emphasizing that God has not cast away His people but has instead preserved a faithful remnant. He argues that the unfaithful Israelites were rejected due to their unbelief, while those who maintain faith, like Paul, remain part of God's promise. The key takeaway is that salvation is based on faithfulness and grace rather than mere genetic lineage or works, highlighting the importance of genuine faith in God's promises.

title: Thinking Right In Romans 10:11-21
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Importance of Spiritual Vigilance and True Faith
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of being spiritually attentive and faithful to God's teachings, as illustrated through Romans 10 and the prophecies of Isaiah. He argues that true belief in Jesus requires more than mere acknowledgment; it necessitates a deep, active relationship with Him, which is evidenced by one's actions and lifestyle. The takeaway is that genuine faith leads to salvation and a transformative relationship with God, while neglecting this relationship results in spiritual blindness and disconnection from God's promises.

title: Thinking Right In Romans 10:1-13
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Justification by Faith: Understanding Romans 10
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores Romans 10:1-13, emphasizing the distinction between justification by faith and justification by works under the law. He argues that true justification comes through a relationship with Christ, rather than through adherence to the law, which can only condemn those who have sinned. The key takeaway is that salvation is accessible to all through faith in Jesus, who fulfills the law's requirements, and that genuine faith involves a heartfelt commitment to obey God.

title: Thinking Right In Romans 9:14 - 10:4
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding God's Justice in Salvation
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores Romans 9:14-10:4, emphasizing God's justice in the context of salvation and the role of Israel as vineyard keepers. He argues against the notion of predestination as understood by Calvinists, asserting that God's mercy and hardening are based on justice, not arbitrary choice. The key takeaway is that salvation is a process that requires continued faith and obedience, rather than a one-time event.

title: Thinking Right In Romans 9:1-16
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding God's Sovereignty and Justice in Romans 9
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores Romans 9:1-16, emphasizing the distinction between God's sovereign choice in selecting Israel as vineyard keepers and the broader salvation program available to all. He critiques Calvinist interpretations of predestination, arguing that God's election is not about individual salvation but about His divine plan and justice. The key takeaway is that God's grace and mercy are extended to all, and His choices reflect His justice rather than partiality.

title: Thinking Right In Romans 8:29-9:7
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding God's Sovereignty and Human Responsibility
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen discusses Romans 8:29-9:7, emphasizing the importance of understanding God's foreknowledge and predestination in relation to human free will. He argues against Calvinist interpretations that suggest predestination negates personal responsibility, asserting that individuals must actively seek God and remain faithful to His calling. The key takeaway is that while God's overarching plan will not be thwarted, individuals have the choice to accept or reject His grace, and daily faithfulness is essential for salvation.

title: Buy The Dip!
speaker: Nathan Bullen
title_alt: Investing in Spiritual Wealth: Buying the Dip
summary: In this sermon, Nathan Bullen discusses the concept of wise investing in both spiritual and worldly contexts, contrasting the behaviors of investors and speculators. He emphasizes that true investors are those who commit to long-term gains based on belief and research, while speculators chase short-term trends and abandon their investments during downturns. The key takeaway is to invest spiritually during life's lows, demonstrating virtue and commitment to God, which ultimately leads to greater spiritual rewards.

title: Thinking Right In Romans 8:18-29
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: From Suffering to Glory: Understanding Romans 8
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores Romans 8:18-29, emphasizing the contrast between present suffering and future glory. He argues that true believers, who are led by the Spirit and willing to suffer for Christ, will ultimately experience redemption and the manifestation of God's kingdom. The takeaway is that enduring suffering is part of the Christian journey, leading to a glorious future that far outweighs current trials.

title: Thinking Right In Romans 8:13-18
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Ongoing Journey of Faith in Romans 8
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores Romans 8:13-18, emphasizing the necessity of ongoing faith and obedience in the Christian life. He argues against the idea of unconditional eternal security and judicial forgiveness, asserting that true salvation requires a continual choice to follow the Spirit rather than the flesh. The key takeaway is that believers must actively engage in their faith to maintain their relationship with God and avoid falling away.

title: Thinking Right In Romans 8:1-14
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Living in the Spirit: Understanding Romans 8
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores Romans 8:1-14, emphasizing the importance of understanding true doctrine and the role of the Holy Spirit in the life of believers. He argues that true conversion and reconciliation with God come from walking in the Spirit, rather than adhering to the law or external practices. The key takeaway is that believers must maintain their justification by living according to the Spirit to avoid condemnation.
themes: the role of the Holy Spirit

title: Thinking Right In Romans 7
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: From Struggle to Victory: Understanding Romans 6-8
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the distinction between the struggles of a person under the law as described in Romans 7:14-25 and the victorious life in the Spirit outlined in Romans 8:1-13. He argues that many misinterpret Paul's experience in Romans 7 as that of a believer, when in fact it reflects the struggle of someone trying to achieve justification through the law without the aid of the Holy Spirit. The key takeaway is the importance of understanding true repentance and the transformative power of the Holy Spirit in achieving victory over sin.

title: Thinking Right In Romans 6-7:6
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Grace, Sin, and Our Identity in Christ
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the relationship between grace, sin, and the law as discussed in Romans 6 and 7. He emphasizes that while grace abounds, it does not permit a lifestyle of unrepentant sin, as true conversion requires a commitment to die to sin and live for Christ. The key takeaway is that believers are called to understand their identity in Christ, which involves rejecting sin and embracing a life of righteousness under grace.

title: Thinking Right In Romans 6:1-23
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Living Righteously: Understanding Grace and Sin in Romans 6
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores Romans 6, emphasizing the relationship between sin, grace, and obedience. He argues that true believers, who are baptized into Christ, should not continue in sin, as they are dead to sin and alive in Christ. The key takeaway is that grace does not permit a lifestyle of sin, but rather empowers believers to live righteously in accordance with God's commands.

title: Thinking Right In Romans 5:1-21
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Justified by Faith: The Path to Reconciliation
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores Romans 5:1-21, emphasizing the theme of justification by faith and the reconciliation with God through Jesus Christ. He argues that true faith leads to a transformative relationship with God, which includes both assurance of salvation and the development of divine qualities such as patience and love. The key takeaway is that believers must actively engage in their faith journey, repenting and trusting in God's promises to experience true reconciliation and peace with Him.

title: Think Right In Romans 4:1-25
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding Justification: Faith, Works, and Grace in Romans 4
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores Romans 4, emphasizing the relationship between faith, works, and grace. He argues that true faith is demonstrated through obedience to God's truth, contrasting it with the idea of earning salvation through works. The key takeaway is that justification comes through faith alone, as exemplified by Abraham, and is available to both Jews and Gentiles alike, highlighting the universal nature of God's grace.

title: Thinking Through Romans 3:1-31
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Justification for All: Understanding Romans 3
summary: In this sermon on Romans 3, Mark Bullen explores the Apostle Paul's message regarding justification by faith, emphasizing that both Jews and Gentiles are equally accountable to God. He addresses the misconceptions held by the Jews about their privileged position and the necessity of faith in Jesus for salvation. The key takeaway is that God's righteousness is available to all who believe, regardless of their background, and that true faith must be accompanied by obedience.

title: Thinking Through Romans 2:1-29
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Danger of Self-Righteousness: Lessons from Romans 2
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores Romans 2:1-29, emphasizing the danger of self-righteousness among Jews who believe their heritage and rituals guarantee their salvation. He argues that true justification comes not from mere knowledge of the law but from obedience and a genuine relationship with God. The key takeaway is that both Jews and Gentiles are accountable to God based on their actions and faith, highlighting the necessity of repentance and living out one's faith.

title: Thinking Through Romans 1:16-32
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Accountability of Truth: Understanding Romans 1
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores Romans 1:16-32, emphasizing the importance of understanding the gospel as the power of God for salvation. He argues that individuals are accountable for the truth they hold and that God's wrath is revealed against those who suppress this truth in unrighteousness. The key takeaway is that justification comes through faith and obedience to God's revealed truth, and that one's deeds should reflect a genuine faith rather than serve as a means of self-justification.

title: Thinking Through Romans
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding the Obedience of Faith in Romans
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the historical context and theological significance of the Book of Romans, emphasizing that it was written by the Apostle Paul to establish a church in Rome that had not yet received apostolic teaching. He argues that the core message of Romans revolves around the 'obedience of faith' and the necessity of living out one's faith in accordance with the teachings of Jesus and the apostles. The takeaway is that true faith is demonstrated through obedience and that the church must uphold the teachings of the apostles as foundational to their practice.

title: When God Throws You A Rope
speaker: Nathan Bullen
title_alt: Are You Willing to Grab the Lifeline?
summary: In this sermon, Nathan Bullen emphasizes the importance of recognizing God's means of salvation, likening it to a lifeline thrown to those who are spiritually drowning. He challenges the audience to consider their willingness to be saved and to grab the 'rope' of God's commandments and reproofs. The key takeaway is that while God is always willing and able to save, individuals must be willing to accept His guidance and instruction to avoid spiritual destruction.

title: The Believer's Safe Place
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Finding Strength in the Joy of the Lord
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of finding joy in the Lord as a spiritual discipline, especially during challenging times. He draws from Nehemiah 8 and Philippians to illustrate that true joy is not superficial but a deep-rooted strength that serves as a fortified place for believers. The key takeaway is that by focusing on God's goodness and promises, believers can cultivate a resilient faith that helps them overcome discouragement and adversity.

title: Jehu, The Reformers & YOU
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Jehu's Legacy: Reforming Faith and Tradition
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the biblical account of Jehu's rise to power and his efforts to reform Israel by eliminating Baal worship. He draws parallels between Jehu's compromises and the historical reformers, emphasizing the importance of fully adhering to God's law rather than settling for comfortable traditions. The key takeaway is the necessity for individuals to examine their own beliefs and practices, ensuring they align with Scripture rather than human traditions.

title: Scriptural Use Of The Keys - Binding & Loosing
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding the Authority of Binding and Loosing
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the biblical concept of 'binding and loosing' as it relates to the authority given to church leaders and the proper application of Scripture. He emphasizes that this authority is not for personal interpretation but must align with God's Word, using examples from Leviticus and the New Testament to illustrate the importance of discernment in church governance. The key takeaway is that true authority in the church comes from faithfully applying Scripture rather than creating new doctrines or practices.

title: Was There A Seed Planted?
speaker: Philip Herr
title_alt: Planting Seeds of Faith: Lessons from David's Life
summary: In this sermon, Philip Herr explores the life of King David, focusing on the traumas he faced and how they may have planted seeds of doubt and failure in his life. The message emphasizes that while David experienced significant hardships, these do not excuse his later actions, particularly regarding Bathsheba. The takeaway is a call for self-reflection on how personal traumas can influence one's faith and actions, encouraging listeners to seek God's help in overcoming doubts and maintaining faith amidst struggles.

title: Resisting The Wedge
speaker: Nathan Bullen
title_alt: Guarding Against Division: The Power of Unity
summary: In this sermon, Nathan Bullen emphasizes the importance of unity within the church and the dangers posed by division, represented by the metaphor of a wedge. He illustrates how pride and jealousy can drive wedges between members, using biblical examples such as David and Saul to demonstrate the consequences of allowing division to occur. The takeaway is a call to recognize our teamwork in Christ and to resist the subtle pressures that threaten to split us apart.

title: Identifying Christ's Bride - Honest Inquiry #7
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Dangers of Idolatry: A Biblical Perspective on Mary and the Pope
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen critiques the veneration of Mary and the authority of the Pope within the Catholic Church, arguing that such practices constitute idolatry and misplace the role of Mary in the Christian faith. He emphasizes that true worship belongs solely to God and warns against the dangers of elevating figures like the Pope or Mary to divine status. The key takeaway is the importance of adhering to biblical teachings regarding worship and the dangers of false narratives that have infiltrated church doctrine.

title: Identifying Christ's Bride - Honest Inquiry #6
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The True Meaning of Communion: Rejecting Counterfeit Priesthood
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen argues against the Roman Catholic Church's teaching on the Eucharist and the role of priests, asserting that the belief in transubstantiation and the continual offering of Christ's body and blood is a distortion of biblical truth. He emphasizes that Jesus instituted communion as a remembrance of His sacrifice, not as a repeated offering for sin, and warns against the dangers of a counterfeit priesthood that claims authority to forgive sins. The takeaway is a call to adhere to Scripture and reject teachings that elevate human authority over Christ's sacrifice.

title: Dentifying Christ's Bride - Honest Inquiry #4
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The True Bride of Christ: A Call to Discernment
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen critiques the claims of the Roman Catholic Church regarding its authority and identity as the bride of Christ. He emphasizes the importance of individual accountability in discerning truth from deception, urging believers to read and interpret the Scriptures for themselves rather than relying on church hierarchy. The key takeaway is the necessity for Christians to adhere to the original Apostolic doctrine and to be vigilant against teachings that deviate from it.

title: Identifying Christ's Bride - Honest Inquiry #3
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The True Bride of Christ: Standing Firm in Apostolic Faith
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the question of whether Christians are bound to follow the doctrines of the Apostles or the teachings of contemporary church organizations. He argues that many modern denominations have deviated from the original apostolic teachings, leading to a potential apostasy. The key takeaway is the importance of adhering to scripture and the teachings of the Apostles, rather than succumbing to the authority of man-made organizations.

title: Identifying Christ's Bride - Honest Inquiry #2
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Discerning the True Bride of Christ: A Call to Biblical Fidelity
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen examines the complexities of identifying the true bride of Christ amidst various church organizations that claim authority and authenticity. He emphasizes the importance of adhering to Scripture and the teachings of the Apostles rather than succumbing to the authority of large, historical church institutions. The key takeaway is the necessity for believers to prioritize biblical truth and personal faith over organizational allegiance, especially in a time of widespread deception.

title: Identifying The Bride - Honest Inquiry #1
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Danger of Misplaced Faith
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of honest inquiry into one's faith and relationship with God, using the story of Israel's defeat by the Philistines in 1 Samuel 4 as a backdrop. He challenges listeners to evaluate their faith and the potential for deception in their religious practices, warning against trusting in rituals or numbers without true obedience to God's word. The key takeaway is the necessity of aligning one's beliefs and actions with Scripture to avoid the pitfalls of misplaced faith.

title: New Covenant - New? Or Renewed?
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding the New Covenant: New or Renewed?
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the distinction between the new covenant and the old covenant, addressing misconceptions propagated by Judaizers and modern interpretations. He emphasizes that the new covenant is fundamentally new, not merely a renewal of the old, and outlines the continuity of God's moral law and redemptive plan throughout scripture. The key takeaway is the importance of understanding the new covenant's unique aspects, such as the new priesthood and the new method of salvation, which are essential for a correct theological perspective.

title: The Spirit Of Submission
speaker: Nathan Bullen
title_alt: The Power of a Submissive Spirit
summary: In this sermon, Nathan Bullen emphasizes the importance of having a submissive spirit, using the story of Daniel in the lion's den as a key example. Daniel's unwavering commitment to obey God, even in the face of danger, illustrates how an excellent spirit can lead to divine protection and favor. The takeaway is that true submission to God involves humility and a willingness to prioritize His will over personal desires or authority figures, ultimately leading to a powerful testimony.

title: From Where Do Questions Come?
speaker: Philip Herr
title_alt: Seeking Divine Answers: The Questions We Ask
summary: In this sermon, Philip Herr explores the nature of questions and the importance of seeking God's guidance, as exemplified in the life of David. He emphasizes that while God is willing to provide answers, individuals often ask with ulterior motives or fail to genuinely seek His will. The sermon highlights the necessity of approaching God with sincerity and the dangers of asking amiss, drawing on biblical examples to illustrate the consequences of not heeding God's clear instructions.

title: Acid Test - Exposing Judaizers
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Grafting of Gentiles: Understanding Early Church Practices
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen addresses the modern-day Judaizers who claim that early Christians adhered strictly to Jewish laws and customs. He argues that the early church, as evidenced in Acts, did not require Gentile believers to follow the Mosaic Law, emphasizing that salvation comes through grace and faith in Christ rather than adherence to Jewish rituals. The key takeaway is that the grafting of Gentiles into the church signifies their inclusion in the body of Christ without the necessity of becoming Jews, challenging the notion that Christianity must align with Judaism.

title: Self Restraint
speaker: Jesse Herr
title_alt: The Power of Obedience: Experiencing God's Nature
summary: In this sermon, Jesse Herr emphasizes the importance of self-restraint and the necessity of adhering to God's commandments as a means to truly know Him. He argues that mere knowledge of Scripture is insufficient; it must be coupled with faith and practice to experience salvation and the divine nature of God. The takeaway is that obedience to God's word fosters a deeper understanding of His character and leads to spiritual growth and good works.

title: Fresh Oil
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Fresh Oil: The Principle, Power and Promise
summary: In this closing message of camp week, Mark Bullen preaches from Psalm 92 — “I shall be anointed with fresh oil.” Saul and David both began with the same anointing of God's Spirit, but David prized it and kept it renewed, and the difference between a believer whose love waxes cold when iniquity abounds and one who endures to the end is a fresh anointing. Using a milk jug that is useless without its lid, and Asaph's recovery in Psalm 73 (“until I went into the sanctuary of God”), he shows that Moses, Joshua, Elijah, David and Jeremiah all came to empty places and needed fresh oil. It cannot be borrowed from others; it is asked, sought and knocked for (Luke 11), and it comes through fresh hones
themes: the anointing of the Holy Spirit

title: Camp: Seeking God
speaker: Jesse Herr
title_alt: Seeking God (partial)
summary: This is a partial recording — only the first roughly fourteen minutes of Jesse Herr's camp message survive on the file, and it breaks off mid-sentence as he turns to 2 Timothy. In what remains, Jesse uses the fable of the blind men and the elephant: each man honestly described the part he happened to touch, but none troubled to learn what the whole animal was. He connects it to the distrust of God's goodness rooted since Eden — the suspicion that God's restraints only withhold good — and to Hebrews 11:6, that whoever comes to God must believe both that He is and that He rewards those who diligently seek Him, valuing Him for who He is rather than merely for escape from punishment.

title: Camp: Courting God
speaker: Nathan Bullen
title_alt: Cultivating a Deeper Relationship with God
summary: In this sermon, Nathan Bullen emphasizes the importance of a genuine relationship with God, likening it to a courtship that requires commitment and self-discipline. He argues that many Christians talk about wanting more of Jesus but fail to take actionable steps towards spiritual growth. The key takeaway is that believers must actively pursue a deeper relationship with God, overcoming sin and false expectations to become 'greatly beloved' in His eyes.

title: Camp: Your Heritage: Good? Or Bad?
speaker: Philip Herr
title_alt: Heritage and the Living Water
summary: In this sermon, Philip Herr explores the concept of heritage and its impact on spiritual identity, using the story of Jesus and the Samaritan woman at the well as a backdrop. He emphasizes the importance of examining one's spiritual roots and the potential corruption of traditions over time, urging listeners to seek the living water of Christ rather than relying solely on inherited beliefs. The key takeaway is the necessity of aligning one's faith with the Word of God to ensure a pure and life-giving spiritual heritage.

title: Camp: Self Discipline Pt 2
speaker: Nathan Bullen
title_alt: The Power of Self-Discipline in Faith
summary: In this sermon, Nathan Bullen emphasizes the importance of self-discipline and integrity in the Christian life. He argues that true repentance requires a genuine commitment to overcoming sin, which is demonstrated through self-discipline and accountability. The takeaway is that believers must actively work to align their actions with their faith, fearing the consequences of their integrity and striving to live righteously.

title: Camp: Self Discipline Pt 1
speaker: Nathan Bullen
title_alt: The True Nature of Grace and Self-Discipline
summary: In this sermon, Nathan Bullen emphasizes the importance of self-discipline and the necessity of denying ungodliness to truly embrace the grace of God. He argues that many Christians misunderstand grace as a license to sin, which leads to spiritual laziness and a lack of growth. The key takeaway is that genuine repentance and a zealous pursuit of righteousness are essential for a fruitful Christian life.

title: Camp: What Did THEY Believe?
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Rediscovering the Faith of the Early Church
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of understanding the early church's beliefs and practices, particularly regarding the relationship between Judaism and Christianity. He argues that many modern theologians overlook the foundational knowledge held by the early Jewish Christians, who were zealous in their adherence to the law while also embracing salvation through faith in Christ. The key takeaway is that true understanding of the New Covenant and Christian doctrine can be found by studying the beliefs of these early believers rather than relying solely on later theological interpretations.

title: Camp: Hinged On The Word #2
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Anchored in Scripture: The Battle for Biblical Authority
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of being anchored in God's Word amidst the ongoing battle against its authority. He argues that true scripture is divinely inspired and must be understood through the lens of apostolic endorsement, rather than through human tradition or interpretation. The takeaway is that believers should rely solely on the Bible as the foundation of their faith and reject any teachings that elevate human authority above scripture.

title: Camp: Hinged On The Word #1
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Anchored in Scripture: The Authority of God's Word
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the necessity of being anchored in God's Word amidst challenges to its authority. He argues that the inspiration of Scripture comes from God through holy men, and stresses the importance of apostolic endorsement for biblical writings. The takeaway is that believers must rely solely on Scripture as the ultimate authority in faith and practice, rejecting any claims of equal authority from religious leaders or traditions.

title: What It Means To Believe
speaker: Nathan Bullen
title_alt: The Depth of True Belief
summary: In this sermon, Nathan Bullen emphasizes the importance of truly believing in God and understanding what that belief entails. He argues that faith is not merely an acknowledgment of God's existence but requires a deep, actionable trust in His words and promises. The takeaway is that genuine belief in Jesus Christ leads to a transformed life that aligns with God's expectations, and it is crucial to recognize the consequences of our actions as reflections of our faith.

title: Camp: The Hindrance - Your Hinge
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Redigging the Wells: Overcoming Spiritual Hindrances
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen discusses the critical hindrance to spiritual growth and understanding, emphasizing the importance of perspective in evaluating one's beliefs. He illustrates how individuals often filter their understanding of scripture and truth through their personal 'hinges' or affiliations, which can lead to misinterpretations and a disconnect from God's intentions. The takeaway is that true alignment with God's will requires a commitment to the original teachings of Christ and the apostles, rather than a selective adherence to modern interpretations.

title: Camp: Re-digging The Wells - WHY?
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Re-digging the Wells of Truth
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of re-digging the wells of truth established by Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, as a means of maintaining faith and covenant with God. He argues that each generation must actively seek to restore these wells, which have been filled with misconceptions and false teachings by societal pressures and spiritual adversaries. The key takeaway is that true sustenance and spiritual life come from engaging with the original truths of Scripture rather than settling for easier, diluted alternatives.

title: Missing The Critical Elements
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Restoring the Divine Nature: The Key to True Fulfillment
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of restoring the divine nature and genuine relationship with God, contrasting it with the superficiality of false worship and modern religious practices. He argues that true fulfillment comes not from external circumstances or possessions, but from a deep reconciliation with God and a pursuit of holiness. The takeaway is that without the divine nature, all efforts to seek happiness and fulfillment are ultimately futile.

title: The Potter & Clay Fable
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding the Potter and the Clay: God's Sovereignty and Human Choice
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the theological implications of the 'potter and clay' metaphor found in Romans 9, arguing against the common interpretation that God arbitrarily determines who will be saved. He emphasizes that God's mercy is contingent upon individual belief and repentance, rather than being a predetermined choice. The key takeaway is that while God has the sovereign right to choose how He works through nations and people groups, individual salvation is based on one's response to God's grace.

title: Thought On Child Rearing
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Raising Godly Children: Four Essential Principles
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen discusses the importance of child rearing, emphasizing that parents must first have a genuine love for God to effectively teach their children. He outlines four key principles: parents must prioritize their own spiritual health, rule with justice and impartiality, actively train their children in the ways of God, and love their children according to biblical standards. The takeaway is that a parent's relationship with God directly influences their children's spiritual development and overall character.

title: Baptism The Meaning & Mode
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding Baptism: Beyond the Mode
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen discusses the significance and various modes of baptism, emphasizing that the choice to be baptized as a disciple of Jesus Christ is paramount. He argues against dogmatic views on the mode of baptism, advocating for a focus on its spiritual meaning and the cleansing it represents. The key takeaway is that baptism is a rite of initiation and symbolic purification, rather than merely a physical act.

title: Life's Unavoidable Realities
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Facing Life's Challenges: Lessons from Jeremiah
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen discusses the unavoidable realities of life through the lens of Jeremiah's struggles, emphasizing that individuals must confront their current challenges to prepare for greater trials ahead. He contrasts the responses of Peter and Judas, highlighting that true repentance and overcoming present issues are crucial for future victories. The key takeaway is that one must actively engage with their spiritual responsibilities and not shy away from the difficulties of life, as these experiences are essential for growth and endurance in faith.

title: Gal 6:6-10 Be Not Deceived...
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Principle of Sowing and Reaping: Understanding God's Justice
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the biblical principle of sowing and reaping, particularly in the context of financial stewardship and moral choices. He argues that our actions, especially regarding money and obedience to God, reflect our true character and faith. The key takeaway is that while God's grace offers forgiveness, it does not erase the natural consequences of our actions; thus, we must be mindful of what we sow in our lives.

title: "Ye Which Are Spiritual..."
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Restoration Through Spirituality
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of sound doctrine and its application in the life of a believer, particularly in the context of restoring those who have fallen into error. He argues that true spirituality is demonstrated through humility and the willingness to bear one another's burdens, as outlined in Galatians 6:1-5. The key takeaway is that one's understanding of doctrine must align with their actions, and that a spiritual person will seek to restore others gently, recognizing their own vulnerabilities.

title: Galatians 5:13-26 Clearing The Fables
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding True Liberty in Christ
summary: In this sermon on Galatians 5:13-26, Mark Bullen emphasizes the distinction between the Mosaic covenant and the liberty found in Christ's priesthood. He argues that true liberty does not equate to freedom from God's moral law, but rather a call to love and serve one another through the Spirit. The key takeaway is that walking in the Spirit aligns believers with God's will, fulfilling the law of love, while cautioning against misinterpreting liberty as a license for selfishness.

title: Galatians 4:1-5:15 Clearing The Fables
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: From Bondage to Sonship: Understanding Galatians
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the transition from the Mosaic law to the heavenly priesthood of Christ as outlined in Galatians. He emphasizes that justification and atonement cannot come from the law, which leads to confusion in understanding grace and faith. The key takeaway is that believers, both Jew and Gentile, must recognize their status as adopted children of God and move beyond the 'childhood' of spiritual understanding to embrace the maturity found in Christ's teachings.

title: Galatians 3:1-4:7 Clearing The Fables
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding Law and Grace in Galatians
summary: In this sermon on Galatians 3:1-4:7, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of understanding the relationship between the law and grace, arguing that many in Christendom misunderstand the role of the law as obsolete or unnecessary. He asserts that the law serves as a guide to faith and highlights that true justification comes through faith in Christ's heavenly priesthood rather than adherence to the earthly priesthood of Judaism. The key takeaway is that reconciliation with God is achieved through faith, not through works of the law.

title: Galatians 3:1-14 Clearing The Fables
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Justification by Faith: Understanding Galatians 3
summary: In this sermon on Galatians 3:1-14, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of understanding justification through faith in Christ's heavenly priesthood rather than adherence to the works of the law associated with Judaism. He argues that adding or subtracting from the gospel frustrates God's grace and leads to a misunderstanding of salvation. The key takeaway is that true justification comes from faith, not from legalistic practices, and believers must remain steadfast in the truth of the gospel to avoid being led astray.

title: Galatians 2 Cleared Of Fables
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding Justification: Faith Over Law
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores Galatians chapter 2, emphasizing the importance of understanding the relationship between the Old and New Covenants. He argues that justification comes through faith in Christ rather than adherence to the Mosaic Law, highlighting the significance of Peter's actions and the implications of compromising the gospel. The key takeaway is that believers must align their consciences with Christ's teachings and not be swayed by traditional scruples or peer pressure.

title: The "Pharisee" Fable
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding the Pharisee: Misconceptions and Truths
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the misconceptions surrounding the Pharisees, emphasizing that they were originally dedicated to preserving the Jewish faith but became corrupted by their traditions and self-righteousness. He argues that many modern Christians mislabel those who uphold biblical truths as Pharisees, while in reality, it is often the accusers who exhibit self-righteousness. The key takeaway is the importance of humility and genuine repentance before God, rather than relying on personal standards of righteousness.

title: The "Filthy Rags" Fable
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Rethinking 'Filthy Rags': The Value of Righteousness
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen critiques the interpretation of Isaiah 64:6, which suggests that all human righteousness is like 'filthy rags' before God. He argues that this view misrepresents God's perspective on good works, emphasizing that while salvation is by grace, obedience and righteous deeds are still valued by God. The key takeaway is that true faith is demonstrated through obedience and that God honors the good works of those who seek Him, regardless of their initial state.

title: Redigging The Wells
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Reclaiming Our Spiritual Heritage
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of redigging the spiritual wells of truth established by biblical figures like Abraham and Isaac. He argues that these wells symbolize the foundational doctrines and teachings necessary for spiritual sustenance, which are often obstructed by false teachings and societal pressures.
