title: Ephesians 3
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Mystery of Unity in Christ
summary: In this sermon on Ephesians 3, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of the church as a unified body of Christ, where both Jews and Gentiles have access to God through the Holy Spirit. He discusses the mystery of the gospel, which reveals that all believers are fellow heirs and partakers of God's promises. The key takeaway is the call for the church to demonstrate God's manifold wisdom through their lives, emphasizing the need for vigilance and preparation against spiritual adversaries.

title: Ephesians 2
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding Our Calling: Grace and Responsibility
summary: In this sermon on Ephesians 2, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of understanding our calling in Christ and the responsibilities that accompany it. He argues that while we are saved by grace, this salvation requires a response of reconciliation with God and a commitment to live according to His will. The key takeaway is that acknowledging our position in Christ must be paired with the active pursuit of holiness and obedience to God's commands.

title: Ephesians 1:5-23
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: God's Plan for Salvation: Understanding Predestination and Inclusion
summary: In this sermon on Ephesians 1:5-23, Mark Bullen emphasizes God's predetermined plan for salvation, highlighting that the inclusion of Gentiles was part of God's original design and not an afterthought. He explains the concept of predestination as God's foreordained plan for redemption through Christ, stressing the importance of personal faith and obedience in remaining part of this plan. The takeaway is that believers are called to recognize their identity as adopted children in God's family, with a responsibility to live according to His will.

title: Ephesians 1:1-5
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding Predestination: A Biblical Perspective
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen critiques Calvinism and its interpretations of predestination and election, arguing that they misrepresent God's justice and love. He emphasizes that God's grace is available to all and that individuals have the responsibility to respond to it. The key takeaway is that true understanding of scripture reveals God's impartiality and the importance of human free will in salvation.

title: It Is Your Life!
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Vital Role of God's Words in Our Lives
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the critical importance of doctrine and the words of God as foundational to the Christian life. He argues that understanding and adhering to God's words is essential for true reconciliation with Him and living a life aligned with His will. The message stresses that neglecting these words leads to spiritual danger and that the covenant relationship with God is maintained through obedience to His commandments.

title: Becoming Bitter Or Blessed
speaker: Jesse Herr
title_alt: From Bitterness to Blessing: Trusting God in Trials
summary: In this sermon, Jesse Herr explores the themes of bitterness and blessing through the lens of biblical characters like Habakkuk, Hannah, and Job. He emphasizes the importance of maintaining faith in God's goodness even in dire circumstances, arguing that true maturity is reflected in one's ability to rejoice in God despite physical hardships. The takeaway is that trusting God as our only hope can prevent bitterness and lead to spiritual growth, even when faced with suffering or loss.

title: They Soon Forgat His Works
speaker: Philip Herr
title_alt: Remembering God's Faithfulness
summary: In this sermon, Philip Herr explores the journey of the Children of Israel from Egypt to the border of Canaan, highlighting their repeated forgetfulness of God's miraculous works and provision. He emphasizes how quickly they went from praising God for their deliverance at the Red Sea to complaining about their circumstances in the wilderness. The key takeaway is the importance of remembering God's past faithfulness to strengthen our faith during difficult times.

title: God Remembers Your Promises
speaker: Nathan Bullen
title_alt: Keeping Promises in Times of Respite
summary: In this sermon, Nathan Bullen emphasizes the importance of keeping promises made to God during times of distress. He uses the example of Pharaoh's hardened heart after relief from the plagues to illustrate how people often forget their commitments once the pressure is lifted. The message encourages honesty with God and highlights the need for genuine transformation and fruitfulness in one's spiritual life, warning against the dangers of making deals with God that are not upheld.

title: Studies In Matthew 27:46-28:20
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Cross and the Resurrection: Understanding Jesus' Final Moments
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the events surrounding the crucifixion and resurrection of Jesus as described in Matthew 27:46-28:20. He emphasizes the significance of Jesus' last words on the cross, the fulfillment of Old Testament prophecies, and the reactions of those present during these pivotal moments. The key takeaway is the importance of understanding the full context of the gospel accounts and recognizing Jesus' sacrifice and resurrection as central to Christian faith.

title: Studies In Matthew 27:1-45
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Betrayal and Crucifixion: Lessons from Matthew 27
summary: In this sermon on Matthew 27:1-45, Mark Bullen explores the events leading to Jesus' crucifixion, focusing on the betrayal by Judas and the hypocrisy of the religious leaders. He emphasizes the importance of discernment in our actions and the dangers of being swayed by emotions or peer pressure. The takeaway is a call for personal integrity and caution in how we influence others, especially in matters of justice and truth.

title: Studies In Matthew 26:46-75
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Facing Trials with Faith: Lessons from Gethsemane
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores Matthew 26:46-75, focusing on Jesus' resolve in Gethsemane and His subsequent arrest. He emphasizes the importance of prayer and preparation in facing life's challenges, as Jesus chose to confront His impending suffering rather than flee. The sermon warns against hypocrisy, drawing parallels between Judas' betrayal and modern-day actions of believers who profess faith but act contrary to it. Ultimately, the message encourages listeners to align their actions with God's will, even in difficult circumstances.

title: Studies In Matthew 26:1-46
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Anointing: A Prelude to Betrayal
summary: In this sermon on Matthew 26:1-46, Mark Bullen explores the events leading up to Jesus' betrayal and crucifixion, emphasizing the significance of Mary anointing Jesus with costly ointment. He discusses the reactions of Judas Iscariot and the chief priests, highlighting themes of faith, betrayal, and the importance of recognizing Jesus' true identity. The takeaway is a reminder to honor Christ and understand the depth of His sacrifice, as well as the dangers of allowing skepticism and pride to cloud one's faith.

title: Studies In Matthew 25
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Preparedness in the Kingdom: Lessons from Matthew 25
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the themes of readiness and accountability as illustrated in Matthew 25. He emphasizes that God is serious about sifting hearts and minds to determine who will spend eternity with Him. The parables of the ten virgins and the talents highlight the importance of being prepared and actively using the gifts God has given us, warning against complacency and false security in faith. The key takeaway is the necessity of enduring in faith and fulfilling one's role in God's plan to be ready for Christ's return.

title: Studies In Matthew 24
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding the Prophecies of Matthew 24
summary: In this sermon on Matthew 24, Mark Bullen explores the prophecy of the destruction of the temple and the signs of the end times as described by Jesus. He emphasizes the importance of understanding the context of Jesus' words, particularly regarding the urgency of heeding warnings about deception and the need for believers to endure in their faith. The takeaway is that true endurance in faith, amidst trials and deceptions, is essential for salvation.

title: Ready For The Trumpet
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding Justification: Ready for the Trumpet
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the concept of justification by faith, emphasizing its significance in understanding one's readiness for the trumpet's sound, particularly in the context of Rosh Hashanah. He contrasts justification by law with justification by faith, illustrating how true righteousness comes from a heart turned towards God rather than mere adherence to the law. The key takeaway is that genuine faith and desire to obey God, even in the absence of the law, is what leads to justification and salvation.

title: Studies In Matthew 22:34 - 23:39
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Heart of the Law: Love as the Foundation of Commandments
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores Jesus's teachings in Matthew 22:34-23:39, emphasizing the importance of understanding the heart behind God's commandments rather than merely adhering to a system of laws. He critiques the Pharisees for their legalistic approach and highlights that true obedience stems from love for God and neighbor. The key takeaway is that love is the foundation of all commandments, and a genuine relationship with God transcends mere ritualistic observance.

title: Studies In Matthew Chapter 22:1-33
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Invitation to the Wedding Feast: A Call to All
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the parable of the wedding feast from Matthew 22:1-33, emphasizing God's redemption program and the invitation to both Jews and Gentiles. He argues that while Israel was initially chosen, their rejection of the invitation led to the inclusion of others who respond with faith. The key takeaway is the importance of being spiritually prepared and responsive to God's call, as mere privilege does not guarantee acceptance in His kingdom.

title: Studies In Matthew Chapter 21
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Triumph of the King: Lessons from Matthew 21
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores Matthew 21 and the events leading up to Jesus' triumphal entry into Jerusalem. He emphasizes the significance of Jesus' foreknowledge and the fulfillment of Old Testament prophecies, particularly regarding Judas' betrayal and the anointing by Mary. The key takeaway is the importance of recognizing the small sins that can lead one away from God, as exemplified by Judas, and the contrast between true devotion and treachery.

title: Studies In Matthew 20:17-34
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Path to True Greatness: Serving in the Kingdom
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the events leading up to Jesus' crucifixion as described in Matthew 20:17-34, emphasizing the importance of humility and servanthood in the Kingdom of God. He highlights the disciples' misunderstanding of Jesus' mission and their desire for positions of power, contrasting it with Jesus' call to serve others. The key takeaway is that true greatness in the Kingdom is found in serving and ministering to others, rather than seeking personal elevation.

title: Studies In Matthew 19:13-20:16
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Covenant and Commitment: Understanding True Evangelism
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the teachings of Jesus in Matthew 19:13-20:16, focusing on the importance of true evangelism and the necessity of being in covenant with God. He emphasizes that salvation is not merely about a one-time prayer but involves a lifelong commitment to following God's commandments and reconciling with Him. The takeaway is that true faith requires active obedience and a sincere desire to align one's life with God's will.

title: Studies In Matthew 19:1-12
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding Divorce Through the Lens of Scripture
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen addresses the complexities surrounding divorce and remarriage as discussed in Matthew 19:1-12, emphasizing the importance of understanding the original context of Scripture. He argues that many interpretations stem from a disconnect with the Jewish roots of the text and a misunderstanding of God's law. The key takeaway is that God's original intention for marriage remains unchanged despite human sin, and that divorce should only be considered in cases of immorality.

title: Studies In Matthew 18
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Heart of a Servant: Lessons from Matthew 18
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores Matthew 18, emphasizing the importance of humility and servanthood in the context of church leadership. He discusses the disciples' desire for greatness and how Jesus teaches that true greatness comes from being a servant and meeting the needs of others. The key takeaway is that a humble heart is essential for effective leadership in God's kingdom, and believers must prioritize serving others over seeking positions of power.

title: Studies In Matthew 17
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Power of Faith and Intercession
summary: This sermon explores the themes of faith, intercession, and the divine nature of Jesus as seen through the interactions of Moses, Elijah, and Christ during the Transfiguration. It emphasizes the importance of faith in overcoming challenges, as demonstrated by the disciples' inability to cast out a demon due to their lack of belief and prayer. The takeaway is that persistent faith and reliance on God through prayer are essential for spiritual power and healing.

title: Studies In Matthew 16
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Leaven of Hypocrisy: Lessons from Matthew 16
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores Matthew 16, emphasizing the importance of spiritual discernment and the dangers of hypocrisy. He highlights the Pharisees' demand for signs as a trap to discredit Jesus, contrasting their skepticism with the faith required of true disciples. The key takeaway is the need to resist the leaven of hypocrisy that diminishes appreciation for God's work and to remain focused on following Christ's teachings without being swayed by worldly opinions.

title: Studies In Matthew 15
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: God's Perspective vs. Human Tradition
summary: In this sermon on Matthew 15, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of maintaining God's perspective over human traditions. He critiques the Pharisees for allowing their oral traditions to overshadow God's commandments, illustrating how this leads to a distorted understanding of spiritual truths. The takeaway is that believers must prioritize God's Word and its intended effects, rather than elevating human interpretations or traditions above it.

title: Studies In Matthew 14
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Cost of True Repentance: Lessons from Herod and John
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the story of Herod Antipas and John the Baptist from Matthew 14, emphasizing the dangers of living by personal standards rather than God's unchanging truth. He argues that true repentance requires submission to a standard outside oneself, which is essential for becoming a child of God. The takeaway is that Christians must remain faithful to God's principles, even in the face of suffering or when others seem to prosper, as God's plans are often beyond human understanding.

title: Studies In Matthew 13:31-58
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Pearl of Great Price: Embracing God's Kingdom
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the parables of the mustard seed and the leaven from Matthew 13, emphasizing the synergistic relationship between human effort and divine action in the growth of God's kingdom. He argues that true discipleship requires forsaking all other 'pearls' to embrace the 'pearl of great price,' which is the kingdom of God. The key takeaway is that genuine faith involves a commitment to prioritize God's kingdom above all else.

title: Studies In Matthew 13:24-43
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Wheat and Tares: Discernment in the Kingdom
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the parable of the wheat and tares from Matthew 13:24-43, emphasizing the importance of discernment in the Christian faith. He warns against the dangers of false teachings and the subtlety of the enemy, who sows tares among the wheat, leading to confusion and spiritual deception. The key takeaway is the necessity for believers to remain vigilant and rooted in the truth of God's Word to avoid being led astray by counterfeit doctrines.

title: Studies In Matthew 13:1-23
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Condition of the Heart: Understanding the Parable of the Sower
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the parable of the sower from Matthew 13:1-23, emphasizing the importance of the condition of one's heart in receiving God's word. He argues that spiritual understanding is not merely an intellectual exercise but a result of consistent choices over time. The takeaway is that individuals must actively cultivate their spiritual lives to truly hear and understand God's message, as neglecting this can lead to spiritual dullness and a hardened heart.

title: Studies In Matthew 12:22-50
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Two Kingdoms: Understanding God's Authority
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the concept of the two kingdoms: the kingdom of God and the kingdom of Satan, as illustrated in Matthew 12:22-50. He emphasizes that Jesus' miracles demonstrate the power of God's kingdom, while the accusations from the Pharisees reveal their alignment with Satan's kingdom. The sermon calls for believers to understand their role as ambassadors of God's kingdom, promoting His governing principles in all areas of life, including politics and society. The key takeaway is the importance of recognizing and proclaiming God's authority and truth in a world often influenced by opposing forces.

title: Studies In Matthew 12:1-21
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Mercy Over Sacrifice: Understanding Discipleship in Matthew 12
summary: In this sermon on Matthew 12:1-21, Mark Bullen explores the nature of discipleship and the conflict between Jesus and the Pharisees regarding Sabbath laws. He emphasizes that Jesus prioritized mercy and human need over rigid adherence to ceremonial laws, illustrating that true discipleship involves understanding God's love and priorities. The takeaway is that following Christ means navigating the balance between law and love, and that true faith is not reactionary but rooted in scriptural principles.

title: Studies In Matthew 11:13-30
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Call to Repentance: Understanding Jesus and John the Baptist
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores Matthew 11:13-30, emphasizing the significance of John the Baptist's ministry and the rejection of Jesus by society. He highlights the importance of recognizing the truth of God's message and warns against the arrogance of wanting God to conform to personal desires. The takeaway is a call to genuine repentance and alignment with God's will, contrasting the responses of those who accept the truth with those who reject it.
topics: the ministry of John the Baptist

title: Studies In Matthew 11:1-12
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding Expectations: John the Baptist and Jesus
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores Matthew 11:1-12, focusing on John the Baptist's doubts about Jesus as the Messiah. He emphasizes how John's expectations of a political savior clashed with Jesus's true mission of spiritual reconciliation. The key takeaway is the importance of aligning our expectations of God with His true nature and purpose, rather than our preconceived notions.

title: Studies In Matthew 10:5-42
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Following God's Instructions: Lessons from Matthew 10
summary: In this sermon on Matthew 10:5-42, Mark Bullen discusses Jesus' instructions to His disciples as they are sent to the lost sheep of Israel. He emphasizes the importance of understanding the context of these instructions, particularly regarding the early church's mission and the distinction between Jews and Gentiles. The key takeaway is the necessity for believers to faithfully follow God's program and instructions, as well as the call to be active disciples rather than passive observers in the faith.

title: Studies In Matthew 10:1-4
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Empowered for the Harvest: Understanding Our Role in God's Work
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores Matthew 10:1-4, emphasizing the importance of being prepared for God's call to labor in His harvest. He discusses how Jesus empowered His disciples for specific missions and contrasts this with the permanent indwelling of the Holy Spirit after Pentecost. The key takeaway is that every individual has a role in God's work, but they must be spiritually prepared and actively seeking Him to be effective laborers.

title: Studies In Matthew Chapter 8:14-34
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Faith in Action: Lessons from Peter's Household
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the theme of faith as demonstrated through various biblical figures, particularly focusing on Peter's household as a ministry hub. He emphasizes the importance of having a supportive spouse in ministry, using Peter's wife as an example of quiet strength and faithfulness. The sermon encourages listeners to embrace their roles within the family and church, highlighting that true faith often manifests in humble service and the willingness to endure hardships for the sake of the Gospel.

title: Studies In Matthew Chapter 8:1-13
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Faith Beyond Borders: Lessons from a Leper and a Centurion
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores Matthew 8:1-13, focusing on the healing of a leper and the faith of a centurion. He emphasizes the importance of recognizing God's authority and the necessity of quarantining sin, drawing parallels between physical and spiritual cleanliness. The takeaway is that true faith and love for God require self-sacrifice and a commitment to righteousness, even in the face of societal challenges.

title: Studies In Matthew Chapter 7:14-29
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Royal Law: Love as the Fulfillment of the Commandments
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen concludes the Sermon on the Mount by emphasizing the importance of the royal law of love, which encapsulates the essence of the commandments. He argues that true righteousness is not merely about following rules but about having a heart aligned with God's purpose, which is to love Him and others. The sermon warns against false prophets and the dangers of legalism, urging believers to focus on a genuine relationship with God rather than mere religious observance.

title: Studied In Matthew Chapter 7:1-14
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding Judgment: The Heart of Jesus' Teachings
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores Matthew 7:1-14, emphasizing the importance of understanding the context of Jesus' teachings on judgment. He argues that while Jesus warns against hypocritical judgment, there are appropriate times for discernment and correction based on God's standards. The key takeaway is the necessity of self-examination before addressing the faults of others, encapsulated in the principle of treating others as one would wish to be treated.

title: Studies In Matthew Chapter 6:9-34
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Living the Lord's Prayer: Aligning Our Lives with God's Will
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores Matthew 6:9-34, emphasizing the importance of aligning one's speech and actions with God's will as expressed in the Lord's Prayer. He warns against the dangers of hypocrisy and the necessity of sincere prayer and forgiveness, highlighting that our words and intentions reflect our relationship with God. The key takeaway is the call to be vigilant in prayer and to seek God's guidance to avoid temptation, while also understanding the principles of forgiveness as modeled by God.

title: Studies In Matthew Chapter 6:1-12
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Living for God's Glory: A Study of Matthew 6
summary: In this sermon on Matthew 6:1-12, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of sincerity in our actions before God, particularly in giving, praying, and fasting. He warns against performing righteous acts for the sake of human recognition, highlighting that true virtue lies in doing these things for God's glory alone. The key takeaway is that God sees our hearts and intentions, and He will reward us accordingly, whether in secret or openly.

title: Studies In Matthew Chapter 5:38-48
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Love and Justice: Understanding Matthew 5:38-48
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen discusses Matthew 5:38-48, emphasizing the importance of understanding God's law through the lens of love. He critiques the Pharisees for misapplying the law by promoting personal vengeance instead of justice and love. The key takeaway is that true adherence to God's law requires love, and that Christians are called to respond to evil not with retaliation, but with a spirit of love and reconciliation, while still upholding justice.

title: Studies In Matthew Chapter 5:27-32
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding God's Law: Beyond the Surface
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores Matthew 5:27-32, emphasizing the true intent of God's law as taught by Jesus, which goes beyond mere external adherence to commandments. He critiques the Pharisees for their selective interpretation of the law, highlighting that true obedience stems from the heart and understanding of God's love. The takeaway is that God's commandments are rooted in love and should guide our actions and desires, warning against the dangers of lust and the consequences of divorce without proper cause.

title: Studies In Matthew Chapter 5:20-26
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Beyond the Letter: True Righteousness in Christ
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of true righteousness as taught by Jesus in Matthew 5:20-26, contrasting it with the superficial righteousness of the Pharisees. He argues that merely adhering to the letter of the law is insufficient; true righteousness involves a heart aligned with God's love and justice. The takeaway is that believers must exceed the righteousness of the Pharisees by embodying God's love and justice in their relationships with others.

title: Studies In Matthew Chapter 5:13-20
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Salt and Light: The Call to Discipleship
summary: In this sermon on Matthew 5:13-20, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of Christians embodying the characteristics of the Beatitudes to be effective 'salt' and 'light' in the world. He argues that true discipleship requires self-examination of one's spiritual state and a commitment to preserving the faith and community. The takeaway is that Christians must actively cultivate their spiritual character to positively influence both the church and the world.

title: Studies In Matthew Chapter 5:1-12
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Beatitudes: Understanding True Blessedness
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the Beatitudes from Matthew 5:1-12, emphasizing Jesus' unique approach to preaching repentance through blessings rather than condemnation. He highlights the characteristics of those who are blessed, such as the poor in spirit, the mournful, and the meek, and connects these traits to the fulfillment of Old Testament prophecies. The key takeaway is that true happiness and blessedness come from a humble and contrite heart that seeks righteousness and mercy, aligning with God's will and law.

title: Studied In Matthew Chapter 4
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Temptation and Trust: Lessons from Jesus in the Wilderness
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores Matthew chapter 4, focusing on Jesus' temptation in the wilderness. He emphasizes that after significant spiritual commitments, believers can expect testing from the devil, who often attacks when they are vulnerable. The key takeaway is the importance of living by every word of God, resisting temptation, and understanding that shortcuts offered by the enemy lead to spiritual compromise.

title: Studies In Matthew Chapter 3
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Preparing the Way: Understanding John's Call to Repentance
summary: In this sermon on Matthew Chapter 3, Mark Bullen emphasizes the ministry of John the Baptist as a call to repentance in anticipation of the coming kingdom of God. He discusses the expectations of the people during John's time and how they were looking for a Messiah to deliver them from oppression. Bullen highlights the importance of understanding God's timing and the nature of His kingdom, urging listeners to remain steadfast in their faith even when God's plans do not align with their expectations.

title: Studies In Matthew Chapter 2
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Magi's Journey: A Call to Recognize the Messiah
summary: In this sermon on Matthew Chapter 2, Mark Bullen explores the significance of the Magi's visit to Jesus and the contrasting responses of the Jewish leaders. He emphasizes the importance of recognizing and appreciating God's work in our lives, as demonstrated by the Magi who traveled great distances to worship the Messiah. The sermon highlights the dangers of complacency in faith and the consequences of ignoring God's revelations, urging listeners to remain vigilant and responsive to God's call.

title: Studies In Matthew 1:2-25
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Genealogy of Grace: Understanding Matthew 1
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the genealogy of Jesus as presented in Matthew 1, emphasizing the significance of the names and stories included. He highlights the inclusion of women and the complexities of their situations, demonstrating how God's grace operates through flawed individuals. The key takeaway is the importance of recognizing our need for a Savior, as Jesus came to save His people from their sins, not just from hell.

title: Studies In Matthew 1:1
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Genealogy of Jesus: A Divine Connection
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the genealogy of Jesus as presented in Matthew 1, emphasizing its significance in understanding Jesus as the fulfillment of Old Testament prophecies. He highlights the dual lineage of Jesus as both the son of Abraham and the son of David, illustrating how these connections affirm His role as the Savior who came to save His people from their sins. The key takeaway is the importance of recognizing Jesus' identity and mission through the lens of Scripture, particularly in the context of Jewish expectations of the Messiah.

title: What God Calls Humility
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Embracing True Humility: From Judgment to Ministry
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen discusses the biblical concept of humility, emphasizing that true humility involves refraining from judgment and focusing on one's own responsibilities rather than criticizing others. He highlights the importance of understanding our role as ministers rather than judges, encouraging listeners to ask what God expects of them in various situations. The key takeaway is that by overcoming our natural inclination to judge, we can better serve others and fulfill our Christian duties.

title: First John Chapter 5
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Avoiding Idolatry: The True Faith in Christ
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the theme of idolatry as presented in 1 John, emphasizing the importance of true belief in Jesus Christ and the necessity of keeping God's commandments. He warns against the dangers of relying on personal interpretations and feelings that contradict Scripture, highlighting that true love for God is demonstrated through obedience to His law. The takeaway is that genuine faith must align with the entirety of God's Word to avoid idolatry and ensure a true relationship with Christ.

title: First John Chapter 3
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding Our Identity as Sons of God
summary: In this sermon on 1 John 3, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of recognizing our identity as children of God and the responsibilities that come with it. He warns against the dangers of Gnosticism and the false wisdom that leads believers away from God's commandments. The key takeaway is that true sonship involves a commitment to righteousness and a rejection of sin, as evidenced by our love for one another and adherence to God's law.

title: First John Chapter 2:12-29
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Deception of Gnosticism and the Call to True Love
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores 1 John 2:12-29, addressing the dangers of Gnosticism and false teachings that undermine the truth of the Gospel. He emphasizes the importance of loving God over the world and warns against the allure of worldly desires, which are rooted in the lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life. The key takeaway is that believers must remain steadfast in their faith and recognize the spirit of Antichrist that seeks to deceive and lead them astray.

title: First John Chapter 2:1-11
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Walking in the Light: Understanding Grace and Obedience
summary: In this sermon on 1 John 2:1-11, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of walking in the light and obeying God's commandments as a demonstration of true faith. He argues that while believers may sin, they have an advocate in Jesus Christ who provides grace and a path to redemption. The key takeaway is that genuine love for God is evidenced by obedience to His law, and that grace does not negate the necessity of following God's commandments.

title: First John Chapter 1
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding 1 John: Confronting Gnosticism
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the context and significance of 1 John, emphasizing the apostle John's confrontation with Gnostic teachings that undermined the nature of Christ and the authority of the apostles. He argues that understanding the historical and theological context is crucial for grasping the true message of the scriptures. The takeaway is the importance of maintaining a correct understanding of God, Jesus, and the apostles to preserve genuine faith and joy in fellowship with God.

title: The Product Of Another's Will
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Molded by the Potter's Hands
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of becoming the product of another's will, specifically God's will, as a path to wisdom and fulfillment. He uses the parable of the two sons from Matthew 21 to illustrate how true obedience to God's design is essential for spiritual growth. The takeaway is that individuals must be willing to submit to God's molding in their lives, rather than pursuing their own desires or agendas.

title: Space To Repent
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Urgency of Repentance
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the concept of 'space to repent' as God's grace and patience towards sinners, illustrated through the story of Jezebel in Revelation. He argues that while God desires to forgive and restore, there is a limit to this grace, and failure to repent can lead to eternal consequences. The takeaway is a call for self-examination and urgency in responding to God's conviction before the opportunity to repent is lost.

title: The Repairer Of The Breach
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Restoring Our Covenant with God
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of repairing the spiritual breaches that develop between God and His people throughout history. He highlights the recurring need for covenant renewal among the Israelites as they strayed from God's commands, drawing parallels to contemporary Christians who may also neglect their covenant with God. The key takeaway is that believers must actively seek to restore their relationship with God by adhering to His laws and teachings, thus becoming 'repairers of the breach.'

title: Study In Hebrews Chapter 13
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Call to Brotherly Love in Hebrews 13
summary: In this sermon on Hebrews 13, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of brotherly love within the church and the necessity of aligning with God's principles for genuine fellowship. He argues that true reconciliation with God involves embracing His laws and purposes, which in turn fosters authentic relationships among believers. The takeaway is that brotherly love is conditional upon shared values and mutual growth in faith, and that genuine love requires accountability and adherence to biblical truth.

title: Study In Hebrews Chapter 12:11-29
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Enduring Correction: The Path to Righteousness
summary: In this sermon on Hebrews 12:11-29, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of enduring God's correction as a sign of true discipleship and love for His law. He argues that suffering is a necessary part of the Christian journey, leading to spiritual growth and eventual glory. The key takeaway is that believers must strive against sin and embrace God's discipline to prove their commitment to righteousness and their place in His kingdom.

title: Study In Hebrews Chapter 12:1-11
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Running the Race of Faith: Lessons from Hebrews 12
summary: In this sermon on Hebrews 12:1-11, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of running the race of faith with endurance, drawing on the examples of biblical figures who faced challenges yet remained faithful. He argues that believers have a superior covenant and are surrounded by a 'cloud of witnesses' who serve as examples of faithfulness. The key takeaway is that each individual must focus on their own race, shedding weights and sins that hinder their progress, and looking to Jesus as the ultimate example of endurance and faithfulness.

title: Study In Hebrews Chapter 11:8-40
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Faithful Living: Lessons from Hebrews 11
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores Hebrews 11:8-40, emphasizing the importance of faith as the primary means of pleasing God. He illustrates how figures like Abraham, Moses, and others exemplified faith through their obedience and endurance despite challenges. The key takeaway is that true faith leads to a longing for a better, godly society and a commitment to live according to God's promises, even when the fulfillment seems distant.

title: Study In Hebrews Chapter 11:1-7
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding Faith: Assurance and Evidence in Hebrews 11
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores Hebrews 11:1-7, emphasizing that true faith is a confident assurance in God's promises and evidence of things not seen. He argues that faith has always been the means of salvation, transcending the Old Testament law and rituals. Bullen highlights the importance of understanding faith not as mere belief but as an active response to God's truth, which is essential for pleasing Him and obtaining righteousness.

title: Study In Hebrews Chapter 10
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Superiority of Christ's Sacrifice
summary: In this sermon on Hebrews chapter 10, Mark Bullen emphasizes the superiority of Christ's sacrifice over the Old Testament sacrifices, explaining that the latter were merely shadows of the true redemption found in Jesus. He argues that true worshippers, who are in covenant with God, should not live with a guilty conscience but rather embrace the assurance of forgiveness through Christ's once-for-all sacrifice. The key takeaway is the importance of maintaining one's covenant relationship with God and the consequences of willful sinning against that covenant.

title: Study In Hebrews Chapter 9
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Superiority of Christ's Priesthood
summary: In this sermon on Hebrews Chapter 9, Mark Bullen emphasizes the significance of Christ as the great high priest in the order of Melchizedek, contrasting the old covenant with the new covenant. He explains how the earthly tabernacle and its sacrifices were mere types pointing to the ultimate sacrifice of Christ, which provides believers direct access to God. The key takeaway is that through Christ's sacrifice, believers can approach God with confidence, experiencing true cleansing and moral transformation.

title: Study In Hebrews Chapter 8
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Eternal High Priest: Transitioning from the Old to the New Covenant
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores Hebrews Chapter 8, emphasizing the transition from the Old Covenant of Levitical priesthood and sacrifices to the New Covenant established by Jesus Christ, the eternal high priest after the order of Melchizedek. He argues that the Old Covenant was a temporary arrangement meant to teach about God's redemption plan, which is fulfilled in Christ, who offers true reconciliation with God. The key takeaway is the importance of understanding one's personal relationship with God through Jesus, independent of earthly religious authorities.

title: Study In Hebrews Chapter 7
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Eternal Priesthood of Melchizedek
summary: The sermon explores the significance of Melchizedek as a priest and king in the context of Abraham's faith and the transition from the Levitical priesthood to the priesthood of Jesus Christ. It emphasizes that Melchizedek represents a higher order of priesthood that is eternal and superior, highlighting the importance of faith combined with action. The key takeaway is that Jesus, as a priest after the order of Melchizedek, offers a better hope and a more direct relationship with God, contrasting with the limitations of the Levitical system.

title: The Testings Of Life
speaker: Jesse Herr
title_alt: Strength Through Testing: Lessons from Scripture
summary: In this sermon, Jesse Herr explores the theme of testing in the lives of biblical figures, particularly focusing on Peter, Abraham, and Moses. He emphasizes that tests are not merely challenges but opportunities for growth and deeper faith. The takeaway is that when faced with trials, believers should remember that stumbling can lead to greater strength and that God's blessings often come after passing significant tests of faith.

title: The Sin Virus
speaker: Nathan Bullen
title_alt: The Spiritual Pandemic: Battling the Sin Virus
summary: In this sermon, Nathan Bullen warns about the dangers of the 'sin virus,' drawing parallels between physical and spiritual health. He emphasizes the importance of maintaining a strong relationship with the Holy Spirit to combat sin and avoid spiritual death. The key takeaway is that believers must actively fight against sin and seek spiritual health, as neglecting this can lead to dire consequences for their spiritual lives.

title: Study In Hebrews Chapter 6
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Growing Beyond the Basics: A Call to Spiritual Maturity
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores Hebrews Chapter 6, emphasizing the importance of spiritual maturity and the dangers of turning away from faith in Christ. He warns against the complacency of believers who remain stagnant in their understanding and practice of faith, urging them to grow beyond elementary teachings. The key takeaway is the necessity of perseverance in faith and the consequences of rejecting Christ after having experienced His grace.

title: Study In Hebrews Chapter 5
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Compassionate High Priest: Understanding Our Role in Christ
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores Hebrews Chapter 5, emphasizing the role of Jesus as the compassionate high priest who understands human suffering and temptation. He argues that Jesus' experiences equip Him to guide and reconcile believers to God, highlighting the importance of sound doctrine and the call for Christians to grow in their faith and understanding. The takeaway is that believers are called to be ambassadors for Christ, representing God accurately and preparing to rule with Him in His kingdom.

title: Study In Hebrews Chapter 4
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Entering God's Rest: A Call to Enduring Faith
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores Hebrews chapter 4, emphasizing the importance of holding fast to faith and the dangers of unbelief as illustrated by the Israelites in the wilderness. He argues that the promise of entering God's rest is conditional upon enduring faith, and warns against the complacency that can lead to spiritual failure. The key takeaway is the urgent call to diligence in faith, ensuring that believers do not fall short of God's promised rest.

title: Study In Hebrews 2:5-3:19
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Supremacy of Christ: Restoring Paradise Lost
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores Hebrews 2:5-3:19, emphasizing the superiority of Christ over angels and His role as the second Adam who restores what was lost through Adam's sin. He argues that Jesus, by becoming flesh, fulfills God's original design for humanity and will ultimately reign over a restored creation. The key takeaway is the importance of holding fast to faith in Christ, who is our high priest and mediator, and the assurance of salvation through Him.

title: Study In Hebrews 1:3-2:4
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Radiating Christ: Understanding His Supremacy
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores Hebrews 1:1-2, emphasizing the supremacy of Christ as the radiance of God's glory and the express image of His person. He argues that Jesus, as the Son of God, is distinct yet of the same essence as the Father, and that believers are called to radiate Christ's character in their lives. The takeaway is the importance of reflecting God's light and character in a world filled with distractions and false expressions of self.

title: Study In Hebrews 1:1-2
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Superiority of Christ: Understanding Hebrews
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the significance of the book of Hebrews, emphasizing its Jewish context and the superiority of Christ over angels, Moses, and Aaron. He argues that understanding the Jewish roots of Christianity is crucial for grasping the true message of the gospel and warns against the dilution of biblical teachings through later Gentile interpretations. The takeaway is the importance of adhering to the original teachings and understanding of Scripture as intended by the apostles.

title: There Is Grace In Your Place
speaker: Philip Herr
title_alt: Finding Grace in Your God-Given Place
summary: In this sermon, Philip Herr emphasizes the importance of maintaining one's God-given place and responsibilities amidst trials and temptations. He uses biblical examples, such as Naboth and Moses, to illustrate that true faithfulness involves staying committed to one's role, even when faced with challenges or the allure of promotions. The key takeaway is that God equips us for our assigned tasks and that we must trust Him to provide grace in difficult situations.

title: What Good Is Your Christianity?
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The True Measure of Faith
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen challenges listeners to examine the authenticity of their faith by asking the question, 'What seek ye?' He emphasizes that many people follow Jesus for personal benefits rather than a true desire for spiritual growth and transformation. The key takeaway is that a faith that does not lead to personal change and sanctification is not a saving faith.

title: When God Gets Tired
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: When God Grows Weary: Understanding Our Responsibilities
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the theme of God's weariness with His people as described in Malachi. He emphasizes that while God has called Israel to a privileged position as His representatives, their fatigue with His requirements leads to His own weariness. The key takeaway is that God's love is not merely unconditional acceptance but encompasses His law and correction, which are essential for maintaining a relationship with Him. The sermon serves as a warning against becoming complacent in faith and neglecting the responsibilities that come with being God's chosen people.

title: The Kingdom NOT Of This World
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Divine Kingdom: Understanding Christ's Authority
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the concept of Jesus' kingdom not being of this world, emphasizing that it is a divine kingdom characterized by meekness, justice, and righteousness. He argues that while Jesus' kingdom is not established through worldly means, it will ultimately manifest on earth with authority and order, contrasting the values of God's kingdom with those of the world. The takeaway is that believers are called to embody the meekness of Christ and ensure that God's purposes are fulfilled in their lives.

title: The Mind That Finds God
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Pursuit of the Mind That Seeks God
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of having the right mindset to truly find God and grow in faith. He contrasts the noble Bereans, who actively sought the truth, with those who cling to erroneous beliefs, illustrating that one's mental attitude significantly impacts their spiritual journey. The key takeaway is that a sincere desire to seek truth and a willingness to change are essential for spiritual maturity and ultimately finding the 'pearl of great price' in Christ.

title: Noble Position Or Noble Person?
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The True Meaning of Nobility: Character vs. Position
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen contrasts the nobility of character with the nobility of position, using the examples of the Bereans and Thessalonians from Acts 17. He argues that true nobility is found in a willingness to seek truth and study the Scriptures, rather than resting on inherited beliefs or positions of power. The key takeaway is the importance of maintaining a noble heart towards God and truth, which allows for spiritual growth and understanding.

title: The Wise Use Of Youth
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Maximizing the Potential of Youth
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen addresses the importance of wisely using one's youth, particularly focusing on young people. He emphasizes that without a purposeful plan for growth and education, youth can easily slip into foolishness and mediocrity. The key takeaway is that young people must actively engage in learning and character development to avoid the pitfalls of a lazy and rebellious society, and that the discipline learned in youth will serve them well in adulthood.

title: Do You Have A Relationship With God?
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding Your Relationship with God
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of having a genuine personal relationship with God, arguing that many people mistakenly believe they have such a relationship without truly understanding its requirements. He outlines four foundational principles necessary for maintaining this relationship: mutual recognition by both parties, genuine love, not befriending God's enemies, and the necessity of agreement. The takeaway is that true relationship with God requires sincerity, commitment, and alignment with His will.

title: Where In This World Are We? Pt 2
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Finding Hope in a Troubled World
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen discusses the sovereignty of God amidst human suffering and the importance of free will in our choices. He emphasizes that while God has predetermined the bounds of our habitation, it is our responsibility to seek Him and make choices that align with His will. The message conveys hope for redemption and the ultimate victory of God's kingdom over evil, encouraging believers to remain steadfast in faith despite worldly challenges.
series: Where in This World Are We

title: Where In This World Are We? Pt 1
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding Our Place in God's Timeline
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the prophetic visions from the Book of Daniel, emphasizing the significance of understanding where we stand in God's timeline. He argues that we are living in the latter days of the fourth kingdom, which is characterized by political turmoil and the anticipation of Christ's return. The key takeaway is that believers should not be discouraged by current events but rather find hope and purpose in the promise of Christ's eternal kingdom that will ultimately prevail over all earthly powers.
series: Where in This World Are We

title: God's Hedge
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding God's Protective Hedge
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the concept of God's protective hedge as illustrated in the story of Job. He emphasizes that Job's godly character and commitment to God allowed him to be hedged in by divine protection, which was essential for his prosperity and safety. The sermon serves as a reminder that maintaining a relationship with God is crucial for spiritual protection against the adversary's attacks, and that authority structures also serve as hedges in our lives.

title: Galatians 6
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Restoration and Responsibility in the Spirit
summary: In this sermon on Galatians 6, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of restoring those who have been led astray by false teachings with a spirit of meekness and humility. He discusses the distinction between the deceiver and the deceived, urging believers to bear one another's burdens and to examine their own lives before judging others. The key takeaway is that true spiritual maturity involves recognizing one's own weaknesses and helping others with compassion, while also understanding the consequences of sowing to the flesh versus sowing to the spirit.

title: Galatians 5
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Freedom in Christ: Walking in the Spirit
summary: In this sermon on Galatians 5, Mark Bullen emphasizes the freedom Christians have in Christ, contrasting it with the bondage of the law and Judaism. He argues that justification comes solely through faith in Jesus, not through adherence to the law or Jewish customs. The key takeaway is that believers are called to walk in the Spirit and serve one another in love, rather than being entangled in legalism or the flesh.

title: Galatians 4
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: From Servants to Sons: Understanding Our Identity in Christ
summary: In this sermon on Galatians 4, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of understanding the transition from the Old Covenant, represented by the Mosaic Law, to the New Covenant established through Christ. He argues that the Old Testament served as a necessary educational tool, preparing believers to appreciate the significance of Christ's sacrifice and priesthood. The key takeaway is that true sonship in God's family comes through embracing Christ and His teachings, rather than reverting to the rituals of the Old Covenant.

title: Galatians 3
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Justification by Faith: The Message of Galatians 3
summary: In this sermon on Galatians 3, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of understanding justification by faith as taught by Paul. He argues against the reliance on the law for salvation, asserting that true faith, like that of Abraham, is characterized by obedience and trust in God's promises. The key takeaway is that believers, both Jews and Gentiles, are justified by faith in Christ, not by adherence to the law.

title: Galatians 2:11-21
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding Justification: Faith Over Law
summary: In this sermon on Galatians 2:11-21, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of understanding the Jewish context of Jesus and the Apostles to avoid false teachings and legalism. He discusses the conflict between Peter and Paul regarding the inclusion of Gentiles and the implications of adhering to the law for justification. The key takeaway is that true justification comes through faith in Christ, not through the works of the law, and that believers must seek to live in accordance with God's moral law while relying on Christ's atonement.

title: Galatians 1:15 - 2:10
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The True Gospel: Understanding Paul's Authority
summary: In this sermon on Galatians 1:15 - 2:10, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of understanding the true gospel as preached by the Apostle Paul, warning against the dangers of accepting distorted versions of the gospel. He highlights Paul's authority as an apostle, which is rooted in a personal revelation from Jesus Christ rather than human tradition. The key takeaway is the necessity of verifying one's beliefs against the original teachings of scripture to avoid spiritual deception.

title: Intro To Galatians: New Covenant
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding the New Covenant: A Deeper Look at Galatians
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the concept of the New Covenant as presented in the Book of Galatians, emphasizing the distinction between the moral and ceremonial aspects of the law. He argues that the New Covenant is established with individuals who willingly accept God's law in their hearts, rather than with the nation of Israel as a whole. The key takeaway is that true believers, both Jews and Gentiles, are those who embrace God's moral law and have a personal relationship with Him, highlighting the importance of understanding the continuity of God's commandments throughout scripture.

title: Intro To Galatians: Earn Vs. Eligible
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding Justification: The Balance of Faith and Obedience
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the themes of justification and atonement as presented in Galatians, emphasizing the difference between being eligible for salvation and earning it through works. He argues that true justification comes through faith and obedience to God, rather than through the observance of the law or rituals. The key takeaway is that believers must maintain their justification by walking in the light and continually seeking forgiveness, rather than relying on a one-time act of faith.

title: The House Of Mourning
speaker: Jesse Herr
title_alt: The Wisdom Found in Mourning
summary: In this sermon, Jesse Herr emphasizes the importance of reflecting on mortality and the value of mourning as a means to gain wisdom and prepare for our own eventual death. He argues that the house of mourning offers insights and a sense of completeness that the house of feasting cannot provide, urging listeners to confront the reality of death to live more purposefully. The takeaway is that engaging with sorrow can lead to spiritual growth and a deeper understanding of life’s purpose.

title: No Vision?
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Importance of Divine Vision
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores Proverbs 29:18, emphasizing the importance of divine revelation and moral guidance in the Christian life. He argues that without a heavenly vision, people can lose sight of God's overarching plan, leading to moral failure. The key takeaway is that while a prophetic vision is valuable, adhering to God's law provides the necessary guidance and happiness, regardless of one's understanding of the big picture.

title: My Ebenezer
speaker: Philip Herr
title_alt: Hitherto Hath the Lord Helped Us
summary: In this sermon, Philip Herr reflects on the significance of raising an 'Ebenezer' as a reminder of God's help and guidance throughout life's challenges. He draws from the biblical account in 1 Samuel 7, emphasizing the importance of turning away from idols and relying on God's strength in times of trial. The key takeaway is that while struggles and temptations may persist, God has been faithful in the past and will continue to provide support for those who trust in Him.

title: Building OUR Ark
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Preparing Our Ark: Lessons from Noah
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen draws parallels between the days of Noah and the present, emphasizing the need for believers to build their own 'ark' through faith and obedience to God's word. He argues that just as Noah found grace by diligently seeking God and following His instructions, modern Christians must also engage actively in their faith to be eligible for God's grace and salvation. The takeaway is that building a strong, biblical community is essential for spiritual survival in the face of impending judgment.

title: 2 Timothy 4
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Staying Engaged in Faith Amidst Challenges
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of maintaining a strong spiritual routine and being engaged in one's faith, drawing parallels between the biblical account of Esther and contemporary challenges faced by Christians. He urges believers to preach the Word and remain steadfast in sound doctrine, warning against the allure of false teachings that compromise true faith. The key takeaway is the call to be vigilant and proactive in living out one's faith, especially in the face of societal pressures and distractions.

title: 2 Timothy 3
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Perilous Times: A Call to Faithfulness
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen discusses the warnings of the Apostle Paul in 2 Timothy 3 about the moral decay and apostasy that will characterize the last days. He emphasizes the dangers of self-love, materialism, and the rejection of sound doctrine, which lead to a corrupt form of Christianity. The key takeaway is the importance of remaining steadfast in true faith and doctrine amidst a society that is increasingly turning away from God.

title: 2 Timothy 2:14-26
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Rightly Dividing the Word: A Call to Sound Doctrine
summary: In this sermon on 2 Timothy 2:14-26, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of focusing on sound doctrine and avoiding unprofitable arguments that lead to division within the church. He urges believers to study the Word of God diligently to rightly divide truth from error, highlighting the dangers of false teachings and the necessity of maintaining purity in doctrine. The key takeaway is that while some issues may seem trivial, the integrity of the Gospel and the unity of the church are worth fighting for.

title: 2 Timothy 2:1-13
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Strength in Grace: Lessons for Ministry from 2 Timothy 2
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of being strong in the grace of Christ Jesus, particularly for ministers like Timothy. He discusses the necessity of enduring hardships as a soldier of Christ, adhering to the principles of the faith once delivered, and the responsibilities of church leaders to preserve and pass on sound doctrine. The takeaway is that true strength and success in ministry come from remaining steadfast in God's grace and fulfilling one's calling without compromise.

title: 2 Timothy Chapter One
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Courage in the Face of Persecution: Lessons from 2 Timothy
summary: In this sermon on 2 Timothy Chapter One, Mark Bullen explores the context of Paul's imprisonment and his relationship with Timothy, emphasizing the importance of courage and faith in the face of persecution. He highlights Paul's encouragement to Timothy to rekindle his spiritual gifts and not to be ashamed of the gospel, even as Christians faced severe trials under Nero's rule. The takeaway is a call to embrace one's faith boldly and to recognize the value of suffering for Christ as a means to eternal glory.

title: Watch Your Wanter
speaker: Philip Herr
title_alt: Guard Your Heart: The Power of Your Desires
summary: In this sermon, Philip Herr emphasizes the importance of being mindful of our desires, or 'wanters,' as they shape our actions and ultimately our destinies. He uses the story of Baelim from Numbers 22 to illustrate how our hearts can lead us astray when we prioritize our own desires over God's will. The key takeaway is to examine what we truly want and ensure that our goals align with godliness, as this will guide us toward a fulfilling and righteous life.

title: I Timothy 4
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Beware of Seducing Spirits: A Call to Sound Doctrine
summary: In this sermon on I Timothy 4, Mark Bullen warns against the dangers of seducing spirits and doctrines of devils that lead many away from the true faith. He emphasizes the importance of sound doctrine and the need for believers to be vigilant against false teachings that can corrupt their understanding of Christianity. The key takeaway is the necessity of grounding oneself in the Word of God and being aware of the subtle ways in which false doctrines can infiltrate the church.

title: I Timothy 3:8-16
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Pillar and Ground of Truth: Qualifications for Church Leadership
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of adhering to God's order and qualifications for church leadership, particularly focusing on the roles of bishops and deacons as outlined in 1 Timothy 3:8-16. He argues that a genuine relationship with God requires obedience to His terms, and that church leaders must exemplify seriousness, integrity, and a commitment to the faith. The takeaway is that the church must uphold its role as the pillar and ground of truth, prioritizing doctrinal fidelity over cultural relevance.

title: I Timothy 3
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Striving for Godly Leadership: Lessons from 1 Timothy 3
summary: In this sermon on 1 Timothy 3, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of character qualifications for church leaders, specifically bishops and deacons, as representatives of the church membership. He argues that aspiring to leadership should be seen positively, as it reflects a desire to serve and uphold the faith. The takeaway is that all church members should strive for the character traits outlined in scripture, as these qualities are essential for effective leadership and the health of the church.

title: I Timothy 2:11-15
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding Biblical Roles: Men, Women, and Authority
summary: In this sermon on 1 Timothy 2:11-15, Mark Bullen emphasizes the biblical roles of men and women, arguing that women should learn in silence and not usurp authority over men in the church. He presents three reasons for this order: the order of creation, the purpose of creation, and the fact that Eve was deceived. The key takeaway is that fulfilling one's God-given role is a matter of protection and efficiency in spiritual matters, rather than a question of equality.

title: True & False Grace
speaker: Nathan Bullen
title_alt: Understanding Grace: The Law of Works vs. The Law of Faith
summary: In this sermon, Nathan Bullen teaches on 'the law of works versus the law of faith' from Romans 3:27, using the message partly to model how he studies — fixing 'foundation stones' (God does not change, God cannot lie, Scripture is God's own word) and reading whole passages rather than isolating verses. Against Marcionism and dispensationalism, he argues that the Old Covenant was never 'the law of works': Abraham, David, Noah, and Moses were all saved by grace through faith exactly as believers are now, and the 'law of works' is simply the false hope of justifying oneself by one's own system or effort, which no flesh can do.
